bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 起著雍灘，盡柔兆執徐，凡九年。

translations.literal: From Juyong Tan through Rouzhao Zhixu; nine years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Juyong Tan through Rouzhao Zhixu—nine years in all.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，上行幸雍，祠五畤。

translations.literal: 1. In winter, the tenth month, the emperor traveled in person to Yong and sacrificed at the Five Altars.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In winter, the tenth month, the emperor went in person to Yong and sacrificed at the Five Altars.

sentences.zh: ----2李少君以祠灶卻老方見上，上尊之。

translations.literal: ----2 Li Shaojun, by means of the stove-sacrifice formula for warding off age, was received by the emperor, and the emperor honored him.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 Li Shaojun presented the emperor with a formula for sacrificing to the stove to ward off old age; the emperor honored him.

sentences.zh: 少君者，故深澤侯舍人，匿其年及其生長，其游以方遍諸侯，無妻子。

translations.literal: Shaojun had formerly been a retainer of Marquis Shenze; he concealed his age and where he had grown up; he traveled with formulas throughout the feudal states and had no wife or children.
translations.idiomatic: Shaojun had once been a retainer of Marquis Shenze. He concealed his age and birthplace, traveled among the feudal states trading in formulas, and had neither wife nor children.

sentences.zh: 人聞其能使物及不死，更饋遺之，常餘金錢、衣食。

translations.literal: When people heard that he could transform things and achieve non-death, they repeatedly sent him gifts, and he constantly had money, food, and clothing to spare.
translations.idiomatic: When people heard he could transform things and cheat death, they showered him with gifts, and he always had money, food, and clothing to spare.

sentences.zh: 人皆以為不治生業而饒給，又不知其何所人，愈信，爭事之。

translations.literal: People all thought that without managing any livelihood he was abundantly supplied, and since they did not know what sort of man he was, they believed him all the more and vied to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: People marveled that he lived in plenty without any visible livelihood, and since no one knew where he came from, they believed him all the more and vied to attend him.

sentences.zh: 少君善為巧發奇中。

translations.literal: Shaojun was skilled at clever utterances that struck uncannily true.
translations.idiomatic: Shaojun had a gift for clever remarks that struck uncannily true.

sentences.zh: 嘗從武安侯飲，坐中有九十餘老人，少君乃言與其大父游射處；

translations.literal: Once, when he followed the Marquis of Wu'an at wine, among those seated were more than ninety old men, and Shaojun spoke of places where he had roamed and shot with their grandfathers;
translations.idiomatic: Once, drinking with the Marquis of Wu'an, he found more than ninety old men at the table and began describing places where he had hunted and shot with their grandfathers;

sentences.zh: 老人為兒時從其大父，識其處，一坐盡驚。

translations.literal: the old men, as boys, had followed their grandfathers and recognized those places—the whole company was astonished.
translations.idiomatic: the old men, as boys, had followed those grandfathers and recognized every place he named—the whole table sat astonished.

sentences.zh: 少君言上曰：「祠灶則致物，致物而丹沙可化為黃金，壽可益，蓬萊仙者可見；

translations.literal: Shaojun told the emperor: "If one sacrifices to the stove, things are summoned; when things are summoned, cinnabar can be transformed into yellow gold, life can be increased, and immortals of Penglai can be seen;
translations.idiomatic: Shaojun told the emperor: "Sacrifice to the stove and you summon things; summon things and cinnabar can become gold, your life can lengthen, and the immortals of Penglai can be seen;

sentences.zh: 見之，以封禪則不死，黃帝是也。

translations.literal: see them, and with feng and shan sacrifices one does not die—Yellow Emperor was such a one.
translations.idiomatic: see them, perform the feng and shan rites, and you will not die—so did the Yellow Emperor.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗游海上，見安期生，食臣棗，大如瓜。

translations.literal: Your servant once roamed the sea and saw Anqi Sheng; he fed your servant jujubes as large as melons.
translations.idiomatic: I once roamed the sea and met Anqi Sheng; he fed me jujubes as large as melons.

sentences.zh: 安期生仙者，通蓬萊中，合則見人，不合則隱。

translations.literal: Anqi Sheng is an immortal who moves through Penglai; when conditions align he appears to men, when they do not he hides.
translations.idiomatic: Anqi Sheng is an immortal who moves through Penglai; when fate aligns he appears, when it does not he vanishes.

sentences.zh: 」於是天子始親祠灶，遣方士入海求蓬萊安期生之屬，而事化丹沙諸藥齊為黃金矣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Son of Heaven first sacrificed to the stove in person, sent masters of the Way into the sea to seek Anqi Sheng and his kind, and busied himself transforming cinnabar and various drugs into yellow gold.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the emperor sacrificed to the stove in person, sent masters of the Way to sea in search of Anqi Sheng and his kind, and set himself to transforming cinnabar and sundry elixirs into gold.

sentences.zh: 居久之，李少君病死，天子以為化去，不死；

translations.literal: After he had dwelt long, Li Shaojun died of illness, yet the Son of Heaven thought he had transformed and departed—not died;
translations.idiomatic: After a long while Li Shaojun fell ill and died, but the emperor believed he had transformed and departed—that he was not dead;

sentences.zh: 而海上燕、齊怪迂之方士多更來言神事矣。

translations.literal: and many eccentric and circuitous masters of the Way from Yan and Qi along the sea came again to speak of divine matters.
translations.idiomatic: and many eccentric masters of the Way from Yan and Qi along the coast came again to speak of divine matters.

sentences.zh: ----3亳人謬忌奏祠太一。

translations.literal: ----3 Miu Ji of Bo memorialized on sacrificing to the Grand One.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 Miu Ji of Bo memorialized that the Grand One should be sacrificed to.

sentences.zh: 方曰：「天神貴者太一，太一佐曰五帝。

translations.literal: His formula said: "Among heavenly spirits the most honored is the Grand One; the Grand One's assistants are called the Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: His formula said: "Among heavenly spirits the most honored is the Grand One; the Grand One's assistants are the Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 」於是天子立其祠長安東南郊。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Son of Heaven established its altar in the southeastern suburbs of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the emperor established its altar in the southeastern suburbs of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: ----4鴈門馬邑豪聶壹，因大行王恢言：「匈奴初和親，親信邊，可誘以利致之，伏兵襲擊，必破之道也。

translations.literal: ----4 Nie Yi, a powerful man of Mayi in Yanmen, through the Grand Herald Wang Hui said: "The Xiongnu have just made peace by marriage and trust the border; they may be lured with profit to come, and with hidden troops we can strike—this is surely the way to break them.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 Nie Yi, a powerful man of Mayi in Yanmen, spoke through the Grand Herald Wang Hui: "The Xiongnu have just sealed a marriage peace and trust the border. Lure them with profit, ambush them, and you will surely break them.

sentences.zh: 」上召問公卿。

translations.literal: " The emperor summoned and questioned the high ministers.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor summoned the high ministers and asked their counsel.

sentences.zh: 王恢曰：「臣聞全代之時，北有強胡之敵，內連中國之兵，然尚得養老、長幼，種樹以時，倉廩常實，匈奴不輕侵也。

translations.literal: Wang Hui said: "Your servant has heard that in the age of complete replacement, though in the north there was the strong enemy of the Hu and within there were successive wars of the central states, yet they could still support the old and raise the young, plant trees in season, and granaries were constantly full—the Xiongnu did not lightly invade.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui said: "I have heard that in the age when Zhao held sway, though the Hu pressed from the north and wars wracked the central states within, people still supported the old and raised the young, planted trees in season, and granaries stayed full—the Xiongnu did not lightly invade.

sentences.zh: 今以陛下之威，海內為一，然匈奴侵盜不已者，無他，以不恐之故耳。

translations.literal: Now by Your Majesty's majesty all within the seas is one, yet the Xiongnu raid and plunder without cease—there is no other reason: because they are not afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Now under Your Majesty's majesty the realm is one, yet the Xiongnu raid without cease—for no other reason than that they do not fear us.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以為擊之便。

translations.literal: Your servant privately thinks that striking them is expedient.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly believe it is expedient to strike them.

sentences.zh: 」韓安國曰：「臣聞高皇帝嘗圍於平城，七日不食；

translations.literal: " Han Anguo said: "Your servant has heard that High Emperor was once besieged at Pingcheng and for seven days ate nothing;
translations.idiomatic: " Han Anguo said: "I have heard that the High Emperor was once besieged at Pingcheng and for seven days ate nothing;

sentences.zh: 及解圍反位，而無忿怒之心。

translations.literal: when the siege was lifted and he returned to the throne, he had no heart of angry resentment.
translations.idiomatic: when the siege lifted and he returned to the throne, he nursed no angry resentment.

sentences.zh: 夫聖人以天下為度者也，不以己私怒傷天下之公，故遣劉敬結和親，至今為五世利。

translations.literal: A sage takes all under Heaven as his measure; he does not let private anger wound the public good of all under Heaven—hence he sent Liu Jing to conclude marriage peace, which to this day has been a benefit for five generations.
translations.idiomatic: A sage measures all things by the good of the realm; he does not let private anger wound the public good. That is why he sent Liu Jing to conclude marriage peace—a benefit for five generations even now.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以為勿擊便。

translations.literal: Your servant privately thinks that not striking is expedient.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly believe it is expedient not to strike.

sentences.zh: 」恢曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Hui said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: " Hui said: "Not so.

sentences.zh: 高帝身被堅執銳，行幾十年，所以不報平城之怨者，非力不能，所以休天下之心也。

translations.literal: High Emperor himself wore hard armor and grasped sharp weapons, campaigning for nearly ten years—the reason he did not repay the grievance of Pingcheng was not that his strength could not, but that he wished to rest the heart of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The High Emperor wore hard armor and grasped sharp weapons, campaigning for nearly ten years. He did not repay the grievance of Pingcheng not because his strength failed, but because he wished to rest the heart of the realm.

sentences.zh: 今邊境數驚，士卒傷死，中國槥車相望，此仁人之所隱也。

translations.literal: Now the borderlands are repeatedly alarmed, soldiers are wounded and killed, and within the central states coffin carts face one another—this is what a humane man would conceal in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Now the borderlands are repeatedly alarmed, soldiers fall wounded and dead, and within the central states coffin carts line the roads—this is what a humane man must grieve in silence.

sentences.zh: 故曰擊之便。

translations.literal: Hence I say that striking is expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Hence I say it is expedient to strike.

sentences.zh: 」安國曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Anguo said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: " Anguo said: "Not so.

sentences.zh: 臣聞用兵者以飽待饑，正治以待其亂，定捨以待其勞；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that one who uses troops waits with fullness for the enemy's hunger, waits with correct governance for their disorder, waits with settled quarters for their exhaustion;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the one who uses troops waits full-fed for the enemy's hunger, waits in good order for their disorder, waits in settled quarters for their exhaustion;

sentences.zh: 故接兵覆眾，伐國墮城，常坐而役敵國，此聖人之兵也。

translations.literal: hence when troops meet, multitudes are overturned; when states are attacked, cities fall—yet one commonly sits and makes the enemy state serve him: this is the army of a sage.
translations.idiomatic: and so when armies meet, multitudes are overturned; when states are attacked, cities fall—yet the sage commonly sits still and makes the enemy state serve him. That is the army of a sage.

sentences.zh: 今將卷甲輕舉，深入長驅，難以為功；

translations.literal: Now if we will roll up armor and move lightly, drive deep and race far, it will be hard to achieve merit;
translations.idiomatic: Now to roll up armor, march lightly, drive deep and race far will be hard to turn to merit;

sentences.zh: 從行則迫脅，衡行則中絕，疾則糧乏，徐則後利，不至千里，人馬乏食。

translations.literal: if we follow in line we are pressed and constrained; if we march crosswise we are cut off in the middle; if swift, grain is lacking; if slow, the rear loses advantage—before reaching a thousand li, men and horses lack food.
translations.idiomatic: march in column and we are pressed and constrained; march crosswise and we are cut off; hurry and grain runs out; linger and the rear loses advantage—before a thousand li, men and horses go hungry.

sentences.zh: 《兵法》曰：『遺人，獲也』，臣故曰勿擊便。

translations.literal: The Art of War says: 'To leave an enemy and gain nothing is to be captured'—your servant therefore says that not striking is expedient.
translations.idiomatic: The Art of War says: 'Leave an enemy behind and gain nothing, and you are the one captured'—I therefore say it is expedient not to strike.

sentences.zh: 」恢曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Hui said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: " Hui said: "Not so.

sentences.zh: 臣今言擊之者，固非發而深入也。

translations.literal: What your servant now speaks of in striking is certainly not to set out and drive deep.
translations.idiomatic: When I speak of striking, I certainly do not mean to set out and drive deep.

sentences.zh: 將順因單于之欲，誘而致之邊，吾選梟騎、壯士陰伏而處以為之備，審遮險阻以為其戒。

translations.literal: We will comply with and follow the chanyu's desire, lure him to come to the border, select fierce horsemen and stalwart warriors to lie hidden in ambush as preparation, and carefully block the dangerous passes as his warning.
translations.idiomatic: We will follow the chanyu's own desire, lure him to the border, choose fierce horsemen and stalwart warriors to lie hidden in ambush, and carefully block the dangerous passes against escape.

sentences.zh: 吾勢已定，或營其左，或營其右，或當其前，或絕其後，單于可禽，百全必取。

translations.literal: Once our disposition is set, we may encamp on his left or encamp on his right, stand in his front or cut off his rear—the chanyu can be captured, and complete success is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Once our disposition is set, we may encamp on his left or right, stand before him or cut off his rear—the chanyu can be captured, and success is certain.

sentences.zh: 」上從恢議。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed Hui's plan.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor followed Hui's plan.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，以御史大夫韓安國為護軍將軍，衛尉李廣為驍騎將軍，太僕公孫賀為輕車將軍，大行王恢為將屯將軍，太中大夫李息為材官將軍，將車騎、材官三十餘萬匿馬邑旁谷中，約單于入馬邑縱兵。

translations.literal: In summer, the sixth month, Grand Counselor Han Anguo was made Protector-General of the Army, Commandant of the Guard Li Guang was made Fierce Cavalry General, Grand Master of the Stud Gongsun He was made Light Chariot General, Grand Herald Wang Hui was made General of Garrisoned Troops, Grand Master of Palace Counsel Li Xi was made Materiel General; they led more than three hundred thousand chariots, cavalry, and materiel troops hidden in the valleys beside Mayi, with the agreement that when the chanyu entered Mayi they would unleash their troops.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth month, Grand Counselor Han Anguo was made Protector-General of the Army, Commandant of the Guard Li Guang Fierce Cavalry General, Grand Master of the Stud Gongsun He Light Chariot General, Grand Herald Wang Hui General of Garrisoned Troops, and Grand Master of Palace Counsel Li Xi Materiel General. They led more than three hundred thousand chariot, cavalry, and materiel troops hidden in the valleys beside Mayi, agreeing that when the chanyu entered Mayi they would unleash their forces.

sentences.zh: 陰使聶壹為間，亡入匈奴，謂單于曰：「吾能斬馬邑令、丞，以城降，財物可盡得。

translations.literal: Secretly they made Nie Yi a spy; he fled into the Xiongnu and told the chanyu: "I can behead the magistrate and assistant of Mayi and surrender the city with it—all goods can be fully obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly they made Nie Yi a spy. He fled into the Xiongnu and told the chanyu: "I can behead the magistrate and assistant of Mayi and surrender the city—all its goods can be yours.

sentences.zh: 」單于愛信，以為然而許之。

translations.literal: " The chanyu was fond of him and trusted him, thought it true, and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " The chanyu took a liking to him, trusted him, believed it, and agreed.

sentences.zh: 聶壹乃詐斬死罪囚，縣其頭馬邑城下，示單于使者為信，曰：「馬邑長吏已死，可急來！

translations.literal: Nie Yi then falsely beheaded a prisoner condemned to death, hung his head below the wall of Mayi, and showed the chanyu's envoy as proof, saying: "The chief officers of Mayi are already dead—come quickly!
translations.idiomatic: Nie Yi then falsely beheaded a prisoner under sentence of death, hung the head below the wall of Mayi, and showed the chanyu's envoy as proof, saying: "The chief officers of Mayi are dead—come quickly!

sentences.zh: 」於是單于穿塞，將十萬騎入武州塞。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the chanyu passed through the frontier pass and led a hundred thousand horsemen into Wuzhou Pass.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the chanyu passed through the frontier pass and led a hundred thousand horsemen into Wuzhou Pass.

sentences.zh: 未至馬邑百餘里，見畜布野而無人牧者，怪之。

translations.literal: When he had not yet reached Mayi by more than a hundred li, he saw livestock spread across the wild with no one herding them and thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: When he was still more than a hundred li from Mayi, he saw livestock spread across the wild with no herdsmen and thought it strange.

sentences.zh: 乃攻亭，得雁門尉史，欲殺之，尉史乃告單于漢兵所居。

translations.literal: He then attacked a signal tower, captured a Yanmen commandery adjutant, and was about to kill him; the adjutant then told the chanyu where the Han troops were posted.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked a signal tower, captured a Yanmen adjutant, and was about to kill him; the adjutant then told the chanyu where the Han troops lay.

sentences.zh: 單于大驚曰：「吾固疑之。

translations.literal: The chanyu said in great alarm: "I had long suspected it.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu cried out in alarm: "I had long suspected it.

sentences.zh: 」乃引兵還，出曰：「吾得尉史，天也！

translations.literal: " He then led his troops back and, as he departed, said: "To obtain this adjutant—this was Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: " He then led his troops back and, as he departed, said: "To obtain this adjutant—that was Heaven!

sentences.zh: 」以尉史為天王。

translations.literal: " He made the adjutant Heavenly King.
translations.idiomatic: " He made the adjutant Heavenly King.

sentences.zh: 塞下傳言單于已去，漢兵追至塞，度弗及，乃皆罷兵。

translations.literal: Below the pass word spread that the chanyu had gone; Han troops pursued to the pass, judged they could not overtake him, and all withdrew their armies.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread below the pass that the chanyu had gone. Han troops pursued to the pass, judged they could not overtake him, and all stood down.

sentences.zh: 王恢主別從代出擊胡輜重，聞單于還，兵多，亦不敢出。

translations.literal: Wang Hui, on a separate command, was to sally from Dai to strike the Xiongnu baggage train; hearing the chanyu had returned with many troops, he also did not dare go out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui, on a separate command, was to sally from Dai against the Xiongnu baggage train; hearing the chanyu had returned with a great host, he too did not dare go out.

sentences.zh: 上怒恢。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry at Hui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious with Hui.

sentences.zh: 恢曰：「始，約為入馬邑城，兵與單于接，而臣擊其輜重，可得利。

translations.literal: Hui said: "At the outset the agreement was that when he entered Mayi city and our troops engaged the chanyu, your servant would strike his baggage train and gain profit.
translations.idiomatic: Hui said: "At the outset we agreed that when he entered Mayi and our troops engaged the chanyu, I would strike his baggage train and gain profit.

sentences.zh: 今單于不至而還，臣以三萬人眾不敵，只取辱。

translations.literal: Now the chanyu did not come but returned; with thirty thousand men your servant could not match him and would only receive disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Now the chanyu never came but turned back; with thirty thousand men I could not match him and would only earn disgrace.

sentences.zh: 固知還而斬，然完陛下士三萬人。

translations.literal: I certainly knew that if I returned I would be beheaded, yet I preserved Your Majesty's thirty thousand soldiers intact.
translations.idiomatic: I knew well that if I returned I would be beheaded, yet I preserved Your Majesty's thirty thousand soldiers intact.

sentences.zh: 」於是下恢廷尉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Hui was handed down to the court commandant.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Hui was handed down to the court commandant.

sentences.zh: 廷尉當「恢逗橈，當斬。

translations.literal: The court commandant judged: "Hui dallied and turned aside—death is the sentence.
translations.idiomatic: The court commandant judged: "Hui dallied and turned aside—death is the sentence.

sentences.zh: 」恢行千金丞相蚡，蚡不敢言上，而言於太后曰：「王恢首為馬邑事，今不成而誅恢，是為匈奴報仇也。

translations.literal: " Hui sent a thousand in gold to Chancellor Fen; Fen did not dare speak to the emperor but spoke to the empress dowager: "Wang Hui was the first to propose the Mayi affair; now that it failed, to execute Hui is to avenge the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: " Hui sent a thousand in gold to Chancellor Fen; Fen did not dare speak to the emperor but told the empress dowager: "Wang Hui was first to propose the Mayi affair; now that it has failed, to execute Hui is to avenge the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 」上朝太后，太后以蚡言告上。

translations.literal: " The emperor attended court before the empress dowager, and the empress dowager told the emperor Fen's words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor attended the empress dowager at court, and she repeated Fen's words to him.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「首為馬邑事者恢，故發天下兵數十萬，從其言為此。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The first to propose the Mayi affair was Hui—therefore I raised several hundred thousand troops from all under Heaven and followed his words to do this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Hui was first to propose the Mayi affair—that is why I raised several hundred thousand troops from across the realm and followed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 且縱單于不可得，恢所部擊其輜重，猶頗可得以慰士大夫心。

translations.literal: Even if we could not obtain the chanyu, when Hui's command struck his baggage train there was still considerable gain by which to comfort the hearts of scholars and officers.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we could not take the chanyu, Hui's command could still have struck the baggage train and brought considerable gain to comfort the hearts of officers and gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 今不誅恢，無以謝天下。

translations.literal: Now if we do not execute Hui, there is no way to answer all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: If I do not execute Hui now, I have no way to answer the realm.

sentences.zh: 」於是恢聞，乃自殺。

translations.literal: " Thereupon, when Hui heard this, he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon, when Hui heard this, he killed himself.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，匈奴絕和親，攻當路塞，往往入盜於漢邊，不可勝數；

translations.literal: From this time forward the Xiongnu broke off marriage peace, attacked the passes on the main routes, and repeatedly entered to plunder on the Han border beyond counting;
translations.idiomatic: From this time forward the Xiongnu broke off marriage peace, attacked the passes on the main routes, and raided the Han border again and again beyond counting;

sentences.zh: 然尚貪樂關市，嗜漢財物；

translations.literal: yet they still greedily delighted in border markets and craved Han goods;
translations.idiomatic: yet they still greedily delighted in border markets and craved Han goods;

sentences.zh: 漢亦關市不絕，以中其意。

translations.literal: Han also did not cut off border markets, thereby hitting their intent.
translations.idiomatic: and Han also kept the border markets open, thereby winning their hearts.

sentences.zh: 1春，河水徙，從頓丘東南流。

translations.literal: 1. In spring, the Yellow River shifted course and flowed southeast from Dunqiu.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, the Yellow River shifted course and flowed southeast from Dunqiu.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，丙子，復決濮陽瓠子，注巨野，通淮、泗，泛郡十六。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on bingzi, it again burst at Huzi in Puyang, poured into Juye, connected with the Huai and Si, and flooded sixteen commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on bingzi, it burst again at Huzi in Puyang, poured into Juye, linked with the Huai and Si, and flooded sixteen commanderies.

sentences.zh: 天子使汲黯、鄭當時發卒十萬塞之，輒復壞。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent Ji An and Zheng Dangshi to raise a hundred thousand laborers to block it, but it repeatedly broke again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Ji An and Zheng Dangshi to raise a hundred thousand laborers to block it, but the dikes repeatedly gave way.

sentences.zh: 是時，田蚡奉邑食鄃，鄃居河北，河決而南，則鄃無水災，邑收多。

translations.literal: At that time Tian Fen's fief for sustenance was fed from Ju; Ju lay north of the river—when the river burst and turned south, Ju had no flood disaster and the fief's receipts were great.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Tian Fen's sustenance fief was fed from Ju, which lay north of the river—when the river burst and turned south, Ju suffered no flood and the fief's receipts swelled.

sentences.zh: 蚡言於上曰：「江、河之決皆天事，未易以人力強塞，塞之未必應天。

translations.literal: Fen said to the emperor: "The bursting of the Yangtze and Yellow rivers are affairs of Heaven; it is not easy to force them blocked by human strength—blocking them may not accord with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Fen told the emperor: "The bursting of the Yangtze and Yellow rivers are Heaven's affairs; it is not easy to force them shut by human strength—blocking them may not accord with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」而望氣用數者亦以為然。

translations.literal: " Those who read vapors and used numerology also thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who read the vapors of heaven and practiced numerology agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是天子久之不復事塞也。

translations.literal: Thereupon for a long time the Son of Heaven did not again attend to blocking.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon for a long time the emperor did not again attend to blocking the river.

sentences.zh: ----2初，孝景時，魏其侯竇嬰為大將軍，武安侯田蚡乃為諸郎，侍酒跪起如子侄。

translations.literal: ----2 At the outset, in the time of Emperor Xiaojing, Marquis of Weiqi Dou Ying was Grand General, and Marquis of Wu'an Tian Fen was among the palace gentlemen, attending at wine and kneeling and rising like a son or nephew.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 At the outset, in Emperor Xiaojing's time, Marquis of Weiqi Dou Ying was Grand General, and Marquis of Wu'an Tian Fen was among the palace gentlemen, attending at wine and kneeling and rising like a son or nephew.

sentences.zh: 已而蚡日益貴幸，為丞相。

translations.literal: Before long Fen daily grew more honored and favored and became Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Fen grew daily more honored and favored and became Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 魏其失勢，賓客益衰，獨故燕相穎陰灌夫不去。

translations.literal: Weiqi lost power, his retainers daily declined, and only Guan Fu of Yingyin, former chancellor of Yan, did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqi lost power, his retainers dwindled, and only Guan Fu of Yingyin, former chancellor of Yan, did not leave him.

sentences.zh: 嬰乃厚遇夫，相為引重，其游如父子然。

translations.literal: Ying treated Fu generously; they drew one another up in mutual esteem, and their association was like father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Ying treated Fu generously; they drew one another up in mutual esteem, and their bond was like father and son.

sentences.zh: 夫為人剛直，使酒，諸有勢在己之右者必陵之；

translations.literal: Fu was by nature stern and upright, given to wine, and toward all who had power above him he would certainly bully;
translations.idiomatic: Fu was stern and upright, given to wine, and bullied anyone with power above him;

sentences.zh: 數因酒忤丞相。

translations.literal: repeatedly because of wine he offended the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: again and again he offended the Chancellor in his cups.

sentences.zh: 丞相乃奏案：「灌夫家屬橫穎川，民苦之。

translations.literal: The Chancellor then memorialized for investigation: "Guan Fu's household and kin tyrannize Yingchuan; the people suffer bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor then memorialized for investigation: "Guan Fu's household tyrannizes Yingchuan; the people suffer bitterly.

sentences.zh: 」收系夫及支屬，皆得棄市罪。

translations.literal: " Fu and his collateral kin were arrested and imprisoned, and all received the death penalty of public execution.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu and his collateral kin were arrested and imprisoned, and all received the death penalty of public execution.

sentences.zh: 魏其上書論救灌夫，上令與武安東朝廷辨之。

translations.literal: Weiqi submitted a memorial arguing to save Guan Fu; the emperor ordered him and Wu'an to debate it east of the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqi submitted a memorial arguing to save Guan Fu; the emperor ordered him and Wu'an to debate it east of the court hall.

sentences.zh: 魏其、武安因互相詆訐。

translations.literal: Weiqi and Wu'an therefore slandered and accused one another.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqi and Wu'an therefore slandered and accused one another.

sentences.zh: 上問朝臣：「兩人孰是？

translations.literal: The emperor asked the court ministers: "Which of the two is right?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the court ministers: "Which of the two is right?

sentences.zh: 」唯汲黯是魏其，韓安國兩以為是；

translations.literal: " Only Ji An sided with Weiqi; Han Anguo said both were right;
translations.idiomatic: " Only Ji An sided with Weiqi; Han Anguo said both were right;

sentences.zh: 鄭當時是魏其，後不敢堅。

translations.literal: Zheng Dangshi sided with Weiqi, but afterward did not dare stand firm.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Dangshi sided with Weiqi, but afterward did not dare stand firm.

sentences.zh: 上怒當時曰：「吾並斬若屬矣。

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said to Dangshi: "I will execute the lot of you together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor snapped at Dangshi: "I will execute the lot of you together.

sentences.zh: 」即罷。

translations.literal: " He immediately dismissed court.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately dismissed court.

sentences.zh: 起，入。

translations.literal: He rose and went in.
translations.idiomatic: He rose and went in.

sentences.zh: 上食太后，太后怒不食，曰：「今我在也，而人皆藉吾弟；

translations.literal: The emperor went to dine with the empress dowager; the empress dowager angrily would not eat and said: "Now while I am still alive, everyone tramples on my younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to dine with the empress dowager; she angrily refused to eat and said: "While I still live, everyone tramples on my younger brother;

sentences.zh: 令我百歲後，皆魚肉之乎！

translations.literal: when I am gone after a hundred years, will you all cut him up like fish on the chopping block!
translations.idiomatic: when I am gone, will you all cut him up like fish on the block!

sentences.zh: 」上不得已，遂族灌夫；

translations.literal: " The emperor, having no choice, then exterminated Guan Fu's clan;
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor, having no choice, then exterminated Guan Fu's clan;

sentences.zh: 使有司案治魏其，得棄市罪。

translations.literal: he sent the responsible offices to investigate and try Weiqi, who received the death penalty of public execution.
translations.idiomatic: he sent the responsible offices to try Weiqi, who received the death penalty of public execution.

sentences.zh: ----1冬，十二月晦，論殺魏其於渭城。

translations.literal: ----1 In winter, on the last day of the twelfth month, Weiqi was sentenced and executed at Weicheng.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In winter, on the last day of the twelfth month, Weiqi was sentenced and executed at Weicheng.

sentences.zh: 春，三月，乙卯，武安侯蚡亦薨。

translations.literal: In spring, the third month, on yimao, Marquis of Wu'an Fen also died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the third month, on yimao, Marquis of Wu'an Fen also died.

sentences.zh: 及淮南王安敗，上聞蚡受安金，有不順語，曰：「使武安侯在者，族矣！

translations.literal: When Huainan King Liu An was defeated, the emperor heard that Fen had received gold from An and spoken disloyal words, and said: "Had the Marquis of Wu'an still been alive, his clan would have been exterminated!
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan King Liu An fell, the emperor heard that Fen had taken gold from An and spoken disloyal words, and said: "Had the Marquis of Wu'an still been alive, his clan would have been exterminated!

sentences.zh: 」----2夏，四月，隕霜殺草。

translations.literal: " ----2 In summer, the fourth month, falling frost killed the grass.
translations.idiomatic: " ----2 In summer, the fourth month, falling frost killed the grass.

sentences.zh: ----3御史大夫安國行丞相事，引，墮車，蹇。

translations.literal: ----3 Grand Secretary Han An Guo was acting as Chancellor; leading [the carriage], he fell from the carriage and was lame.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 Grand Secretary Han An Guo was acting as Chancellor; while leading the carriage he fell from it and was lame.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁巳，以平棘侯薛澤為丞相，安國病免。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on dingsi, Marquis of Pingji Xue Ze was made Chancellor; An Guo was removed for illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dingsi, Marquis of Pingji Xue Ze was made Chancellor, and An Guo was dismissed on account of illness.

translations.literal: ----4 An earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 An earthquake.

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: An amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: ----5九月，以中尉張歐為御史大夫。

translations.literal: ----5 In the ninth month, Commandant of the Guards Zhang Ou was made Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In the ninth month, Commandant of the Guards Zhang Ou was made Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 韓安國疾愈，復為中尉。

translations.literal: Han An Guo recovered from illness and again became Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Han An Guo recovered from illness and again became Commandant of the Guards.

sentences.zh: ----6河間王德，修學好古，實事求是，以金帛招求四方善書，得書多，與漢朝等。

translations.literal: ----6 King De of Hejian studied the classics and loved antiquity, sought truth from facts in practical affairs, and used gold and silk to recruit good books from all quarters; the books he obtained were many and equal to the Han court's.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 King De of Hejian studied the classics and loved antiquity, sought truth from facts, and used gold and silk to recruit good books from all quarters; the books he obtained were as many as the Han court's.

sentences.zh: 是時，淮南王安亦好書，所招致率多浮辯。

translations.literal: At that time King An of Huainan also loved books, but those he recruited were mostly empty disputations.
translations.idiomatic: At that time King An of Huainan also loved books, but those he recruited were mostly empty disputations.

sentences.zh: 獻王所得書，皆古文、先秦舊書，采禮樂古事，稍稍增輯至五百餘篇，被服、造次必於儒者，山東諸儒多從之遊。

translations.literal: The books obtained by Prince Xian were all ancient script and pre-Qin old books; he gathered ancient matters of ritual and music and gradually compiled and added to more than five hundred chapters; in dress and bearing he always conformed to Confucians, and the Confucians of Shandong mostly followed him to study.
translations.idiomatic: The books Prince Xian obtained were all ancient script and pre-Qin old books; he gathered ancient matters of ritual and music and gradually compiled more than five hundred chapters; in dress and bearing he always conformed to Confucians, and the Confucians of Shandong mostly followed him to study.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，河間王來朝，獻雅樂，對三雍宮及詔策所問三十餘事。

translations.literal: 1 In winter, the tenth month, the King of Hejian came to court, presented elegant music, and answered more than thirty items at the Three Yong Palace and in the imperial questions and policy.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In winter, the tenth month, the King of Hejian came to court, presented elegant music, and answered more than thirty items at the Three Yong Palace and in the imperial questions and policy.

sentences.zh: 其對，推道術而言，得事之中，文約指明。

translations.literal: His answers, pushing the Way and its techniques in speech, hit the middle of affairs; the text was sparse yet pointed clearly.
translations.idiomatic: His answers, expounding the Way and its techniques, hit the middle of affairs; the text was spare yet pointed clearly.

sentences.zh: 天子下太樂官常存肄河間王所獻雅聲，歲時以備數，然不常御也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven ordered the Director of Imperial Music always to keep and practice the elegant tones that the King of Hejian had presented, each year for the full complement of performances, yet they were not regularly performed at court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Director of Imperial Music always to keep and practice the elegant tones the King of Hejian had presented, each year for the full complement of performances, yet they were not regularly performed at court.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，河間王薨，中尉常麗以聞，曰：「王身端行治，溫仁恭儉，篤敬愛下，明知深察，惠於鰥寡。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the King of Hejian died; Commandant of the Guards Chang Li reported, saying: "The king's person was upright in conduct and governance, warm, benevolent, respectful and frugal, sincerely respectful and loving to subordinates, clearly perceptive and deeply observant, and kind to widows and orphans.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the King of Hejian died; Commandant of the Guards Chang Li reported, saying, "The king's person was upright in conduct and governance, warm, benevolent, respectful and frugal, sincerely respectful and loving to subordinates, clearly perceptive and deeply observant, and kind to widows and orphans.

sentences.zh: 」大行令奏：「謚法：『聰明睿知曰獻，』謚曰獻王。

translations.literal: " The Grand Herald submitted: "Posthumous standards: 'Intelligent and perspicacious is called Xian,'" and the posthumous title was King Xian.
translations.idiomatic: " The Grand Herald submitted, "Posthumous standards: 'Intelligent and perspicacious is called Xian,'" and the posthumous title was King Xian.

sentences.zh: ::班固贊曰：昔魯哀公有言：「寡人生於深宮之中，長於婦人之手，未嘗知憂，未嘗知懼。

translations.literal: :: Ban Gu's praise says: Formerly Duke Ai of Lu had a saying: "I was born in the deep palace, raised in women's hands, never knew worry, never knew fear.
translations.idiomatic: :: Ban Gu's praise says: Formerly Duke Ai of Lu had a saying, "I was born in the deep palace, raised in women's hands, never knew worry, never knew fear.

sentences.zh: 」信哉斯言也，雖欲不危亡，不可得已！

translations.literal: " Truly that saying! Though wishing not to perish, it cannot be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: " Truly that saying! Though one wishes not to perish, it cannot be obtained!

sentences.zh: 是故古人以宴安為鴆毒，無德而富貴謂之不幸。

translations.literal: Therefore the ancients took ease and peace as poisoned wine, and wealth and honor without virtue they called misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the ancients took ease and peace as poisoned wine, and wealth and honor without virtue they called misfortune.

sentences.zh: 漢興，至於孝平，諸侯王以百數，率多驕淫失道。

translations.literal: From Han's rise down to Emperor Ping, feudal kings numbered in the hundreds, and most were arrogant, licentious, and lost the Way.
translations.idiomatic: From Han's rise down to Emperor Ping, feudal kings numbered in the hundreds, and most were arrogant, licentious, and lost the Way.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 沈溺放恣之中，居勢使然也。

translations.literal: Drowned in indulgence and license—their position made it so.
translations.idiomatic: Drowned in indulgence and license—their position made it so.

sentences.zh: 自凡人猶繫於習俗，而況哀公之倫乎！

translations.literal: Even ordinary men are bound by custom and habit—how much more the class of Duke Ai!
translations.idiomatic: Even ordinary men are bound by custom and habit—how much more the class of Duke Ai!

sentences.zh: 「夫唯大雅，卓爾不群」，河間獻王近之矣。

translations.literal: "Only the great elegant, outstanding and not of the crowd"—Prince Xian of Hejian approached this.
translations.idiomatic: "Only the great elegant, outstanding and not of the crowd"—Prince Xian of Hejian approached this.

translations.literal: ----2 At the outset, when Wang Hui attacked Eastern Yue, he sent the magistrate of Poyang, Tang Meng, to inform Southern Yue by letter.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 At the outset, when Wang Hui attacked Eastern Yue, he sent the magistrate of Poyang, Tang Meng, to inform Southern Yue by letter.

sentences.zh: 南越食蒙以蜀枸醬，蒙問所從來。

translations.literal: Southern Yue fed Meng with Shu zha sauce; Meng asked where it came from.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Yue fed Meng with Shu zha sauce; Meng asked where it came from.

sentences.zh: 曰：「道西北牂柯江。

translations.literal: They said: "The route is northwest via the Zangke River.
translations.idiomatic: They said, "The route is northwest via the Zangke River.

sentences.zh: 牂柯江廣數里，出番禺城下。

translations.literal: The Zangke River is several li wide and emerges below Panyu city.
translations.idiomatic: The Zangke River is several li wide and emerges below Panyu city.

translations.literal: " Meng returned to Chang'an and questioned Shu merchants.
translations.idiomatic: " Meng returned to Chang'an and questioned Shu merchants.

sentences.zh: 賈人曰：「獨蜀出枸醬，多持竊出市夜郎。

translations.literal: The merchants said: "Only Shu produces zha sauce; many secretly carry it out to sell at Yelang.
translations.idiomatic: The merchants said, "Only Shu produces zha sauce; many secretly carry it out to sell at Yelang.

sentences.zh: 夜郎者，臨牂柯江，江廣百餘步，足以行船。

translations.literal: Yelang borders the Zangke River; the river is over a hundred paces wide, enough for boats to travel.
translations.idiomatic: Yelang borders the Zangke River; the river is over a hundred paces wide, enough for boats to travel.

sentences.zh: 南越以財物役屬夜郎，西至桐師，然亦不能臣使也。

translations.literal: Southern Yue used goods to subordinate Yelang, west to Tongshi, yet also could not make them subjects and servants.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Yue used goods to subordinate Yelang, west to Tongshi, yet also could not make them subjects and servants.

sentences.zh: 」蒙乃上書說上曰：「南越王黃屋左纛，地東西萬餘里，名為外臣，實一州主也。

translations.literal: " Meng then memorialized persuading the emperor, saying: "The King of Southern Yue has a yellow canopy and left banner, territory east and west over ten thousand li, named an outer subject but in truth master of a whole province.
translations.idiomatic: " Meng then memorialized persuading the emperor, saying, "The King of Southern Yue has a yellow canopy and left banner, territory east and west over ten thousand li, named an outer subject but in truth master of a whole province.

sentences.zh: 今以長沙、豫章往，水道多絕，難行。

translations.literal: Now going from Changsha and Yuzhang, the waterways are mostly cut off and hard to travel.
translations.idiomatic: Now going from Changsha and Yuzhang, the waterways are mostly cut off and hard to travel.

sentences.zh: 竊聞夜郎所有精兵可得十餘萬，浮船牂柯江，出其不意，此制越一奇也。

translations.literal: I have heard that Yelang has crack troops that can be obtained, over a hundred thousand; float boats on the Zangke River and take them by surprise—this is one wondrous stratagem for controlling Yue.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Yelang has crack troops numbering over a hundred thousand; float boats on the Zangke River and take them by surprise—this is one wondrous stratagem for controlling Yue.

sentences.zh: 誠以漢之強，巴、蜀之饒，通夜郎道為置吏，甚易。

translations.literal: Truly with Han's strength and Ba-Shu's abundance, opening the road to Yelang and placing officials is very easy.
translations.idiomatic: Truly with Han's strength and Ba-Shu's abundance, opening the road to Yelang and placing officials is very easy.

sentences.zh: 」上許之。

translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

translations.literal: He thereupon appointed Meng as General of the Gentlemen of the Palace, leading a thousand men and provisions for over ten thousand, entering from the Zam Pass of Ba-Shu, and then met the Marquis of Yelang, Duotong.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon appointed Meng as General of the Gentlemen of the Palace, leading a thousand men and provisions for over ten thousand, entering from the Zam Pass of Ba-Shu, and then met the Marquis of Yelang, Duotong.

translations.literal: Meng richly rewarded him, instructed him with prestige and virtue, agreed to place officials, and made his son a magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Meng richly rewarded him, instructed him with prestige and virtue, agreed to place officials, and made his son a magistrate.

translations.literal: The small towns beside Yelang all coveted Han silk; they thought the Han road was dangerous and that Han ultimately could not possess them, and for the time being listened to Meng's agreement.
translations.idiomatic: The small towns beside Yelang all coveted Han silk; they thought the Han road was dangerous and that Han ultimately could not possess them, and for the time being listened to Meng's agreement.

translations.literal: On returning to report, the emperor made it the commandery of Qianwei and sent Ba-Shu soldiers to build the road from Bo finger to the Zangke River; workers numbered tens of thousands, soldiers suffered many casualties, and there were deserters.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to report, the emperor made it the commandery of Qianwei and sent Ba-Shu soldiers to build the road from Bo finger to the Zangke River; workers numbered tens of thousands, soldiers suffered many casualties, and there were deserters.

translations.idiomatic: Using the war-levies law, he executed the ringleaders, and the people of Ba-Shu were greatly terrified.

translations.literal: Xiangru returned and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangru returned and reported.

translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Hong of Zichuan answered in the policy examination, saying:

sentences.zh: :「臣聞上古堯、舜之時，不貴爵賞而民勸善，不重刑罰而民不犯，躬率以正則遇民信也；

translations.literal: : "Your servant has heard that in high antiquity in the time of Yao and Shun, they did not value ranks and rewards yet the people were encouraged to goodness, did not emphasize punishments yet the people did not offend; personally leading with rectitude, they met with the people's trust;
translations.idiomatic: : "Your servant has heard that in high antiquity in the time of Yao and Shun, they did not value ranks and rewards yet the people were encouraged to goodness, did not emphasize punishments yet the people did not offend; personally leading with rectitude, they met with the people's trust;

sentences.zh: 末世貴爵厚賞而民不勸，深刑重罰而奸不止，其上不正，遇民不信也。

translations.literal: in the degenerate age they valued ranks and thick rewards yet the people were not encouraged, used deep punishments and heavy penalties yet wickedness did not stop; those above were not upright, and they met with the people's distrust.
translations.idiomatic: in the degenerate age they valued ranks and thick rewards yet the people were not encouraged, used deep punishments and heavy penalties yet wickedness did not stop; those above were not upright, and they met with the people's distrust.

sentences.zh: 夫厚賞重刑，未足以勸善而禁非，必信而已矣。

translations.literal: Thick rewards and heavy punishments are not enough to encourage goodness and forbid wrongdoing—trust alone suffices.
translations.idiomatic: Thick rewards and heavy punishments are not enough to encourage goodness and forbid wrongdoing—trust alone suffices.

sentences.zh: 是故因能任官，則分職治；

translations.literal: Therefore, appointing offices according to ability, then duties are divided and governed;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, appointing offices according to ability, then duties are divided and governed;

sentences.zh: 去無用之言，則事情得；

translations.literal: removing useless words, then affairs are obtained;
translations.idiomatic: removing useless words, then affairs are obtained;

translations.literal: not making useless implements, then levies and collections are reduced;
translations.idiomatic: not making useless implements, then levies and collections are reduced;

sentences.zh: 不奪民時，不妨民力，則百姓富；

translations.literal: not seizing the people's seasons, not obstructing the people's strength, then the hundred surnames are rich;
translations.idiomatic: not seizing the people's seasons, not obstructing the people's strength, then the hundred surnames are rich;

translations.idiomatic: the virtuous advance, the without-virtue retreat, then the court is honored;

sentences.zh: 有功者上，無功者下，則群臣逡；

translations.literal: the meritorious rise, the without-merit descend, then the ministers shrink back;
translations.idiomatic: the meritorious rise, the without-merit descend, then the ministers shrink back;

sentences.zh: 罰當罪，則奸邪止；

translations.literal: punishments match crimes, then wickedness stops;
translations.idiomatic: punishments match crimes, then wickedness stops;

sentences.zh: 賞當賢，則臣下勸。

translations.literal: rewards match worthiness, then subordinates are encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: rewards match worthiness, then subordinates are encouraged.

sentences.zh: 凡此八者，治之本也。

translations.literal: All these eight are the root of governance.
translations.idiomatic: All these eight are the root of governance.

sentences.zh: 故民者，業之則不爭，理得則不怨，有禮則不暴，愛之則親上，此有天下之急者也。

translations.literal: Therefore the people, given occupations then do not contend, when principle is obtained then do not resent, when there is ritual then are not violent, when loved then are close to superiors—this is what those who possess all under Heaven urgently need.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the people, given occupations then do not contend, when principle is obtained then do not resent, when there is ritual then are not violent, when loved then are close to superiors—this is what those who possess all under Heaven urgently need.

sentences.zh: 禮義者，民之所服也；

translations.literal: Ritual and righteousness are what the people submit to;
translations.idiomatic: Ritual and righteousness are what the people submit to;

sentences.zh: 而賞罰順之，則民不犯禁矣。

translations.literal: And when rewards and punishments accord with it, then the people do not violate prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: And when rewards and punishments accord with it, the people will not violate prohibitions.

sentences.zh: :「臣聞之：氣同則從，聲比則應。

translations.literal: : "Your servant has heard: when qi is the same, they follow; when sounds match, they respond.
translations.idiomatic: : "Your servant has heard: when qi is the same, they follow; when sounds match, they respond.

sentences.zh: 今人主和德於上，百姓和合於下，故心和則氣和，氣和則形和，形和則聲和，聲和則天地之和應矣。

translations.literal: Now when the ruler harmonizes virtue above and the hundred surnames unite in harmony below, therefore when the heart is harmonious then qi is harmonious, when qi is harmonious then form is harmonious, when form is harmonious then sound is harmonious, when sound is harmonious then Heaven and Earth's harmony responds.
translations.idiomatic: Now when the ruler harmonizes virtue above and the people unite in harmony below, therefore when the heart is harmonious then qi is harmonious, when qi is harmonious then form is harmonious, when form is harmonious then sound is harmonious, when sound is harmonious then Heaven and Earth's harmony responds.

sentences.zh: 故陰陽和，風雨時，甘露降，五穀登，六畜蕃，嘉禾興，朱草生，山不童，澤不涸，此和之至也。

translations.literal: Therefore yin and yang harmonize, wind and rain are timely, sweet dew descends, the five grains rise, the six livestock multiply, fine grain flourishes, cinnabar grass grows, mountains are not bald, marshes are not dry—this is harmony at its utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore yin and yang harmonize, wind and rain are timely, sweet dew descends, the five grains ripen, livestock multiply, fine grain flourishes, cinnabar grass grows, mountains are not stripped bare, marshes do not dry up—this is harmony at its utmost.

sentences.zh: 策奏，天子擢弘對為第一，拜為博士，待詔金馬門。

translations.idiomatic: When the examination responses were presented, the Son of Heaven elevated Hong's answer to first place, appointed him Erudite, and made him await edicts at the Golden Horse Gate.

translations.idiomatic: " Many scholars mostly slandered and attacked Gu; Gu thereupon, on account of age, was dismissed and returned home.

translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the emperor observed his conduct was cautious and solid, his disputation ample, he was skilled in legal documents and clerk affairs and adorned them with Confucian arts—the emperor was greatly pleased and within one year promoted him to Left Metropolitan Superintendent.
