translations.literal: The High Emperor probably regretted it deeply and then sent Liu Jing to go and conclude the marriage-alliance treaty; after that all under Heaven forgot affairs of spear and shield.
translations.idiomatic: The High Emperor probably regretted it deeply and then sent Liu Jing to go and conclude the marriage-alliance treaty; after that all under Heaven forgot affairs of spear and shield.

sentences.zh: :「夫匈奴難得而制，非一世也；

translations.literal: : "Now the Xiongnu are hard to obtain and control—not for one generation alone;
translations.idiomatic: : "The Xiongnu are hard to seize and control, and this has been so for generations;

sentences.zh: 行盜侵驅，所以為業也，天性固然。

translations.literal: roaming robbery, invasion, and driving—this is their calling; by nature it is thus solid.
translations.idiomatic: raiding, plundering, and harrying are their trade; it is so by their nature.

sentences.zh: 上及虞、夏、殷、周，固弗程督，禽獸畜之，不屬為人。

translations.literal: Up through Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou, they solidly did not supervise by regulations, kept them like birds and beasts, not making them belong as people.
translations.idiomatic: Through Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou, rulers did not regulate them by law but kept them like birds and beasts, not as subjects.

sentences.zh: 夫上不觀虞、夏、殷、周之流，而下循近世之失，此臣之所大憂，百姓之所疾苦也。

translations.literal: Not looking above at the stream of Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou, yet below following recent generations' failures—this is what your servant greatly fears and what the hundred surnames suffer as hardship.
translations.idiomatic: To ignore the example of Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou yet below follow the mistakes of recent times—this is what your servant greatly fears and what afflicts the common people.

sentences.zh: 嚴安上書曰：

translations.literal: Yan An submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yan An submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: :「今天下人民，用財侈靡，車馬、衣裘、宮室，皆競修飾，調五聲使有節族，雜五色使有文章，重五味方丈於前，以觀欲天下。

translations.literal: : "Now the people of all under Heaven use wealth in extravagant excess; chariots and horses, fur garments, and palaces all vie in ornament; the five tones are tuned to have measure and cadence, the five colors mixed to have pattern and design, the five flavors piled a square zhang before one, to display desire to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: : "Now the people of the realm spend wealth with extravagant excess; chariots and horses, fur robes, and palaces all vie in ornament; the five tones are tuned to measured cadence, the five colors blended into patterned display, the five flavors heaped a full table's breadth before one—to parade desire before all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 彼民之情，見美則願之，是教民以侈也；

translations.literal: Those people's disposition—seeing beauty they then desire it—this is teaching the people excess;
translations.idiomatic: When the people see beauty they desire it—this is teaching the people extravagance;

sentences.zh: 侈而無節，則不可贍，民離本而徼末矣。

translations.literal: excess without measure, then cannot be supplied; the people leave the root and grasp at the branch tips.
translations.idiomatic: extravagance without restraint cannot be sustained; the people leave the root and grasp at the branch tips.

sentences.zh: 末不可徒得，故縉紳者不憚為詐，帶劍者誇殺人以矯奪，而世不知愧，是以犯法者眾。

translations.literal: Branch tips cannot be obtained in vain; therefore girdled-sash gentlemen do not fear practicing fraud, sword-bearing men boast killing people to seize by force, yet the age does not know shame—thus lawbreakers are many.
translations.idiomatic: the branch tips cannot be had for nothing; therefore gentry do not fear fraud, sword-bearing men boast of killing to seize by force, yet the age feels no shame—thus lawbreakers are many.

sentences.zh: 臣願為民制度以防其淫，使貧富不相燿以和其心；

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to make institutions for the people to guard against their excess, causing poor and rich not to dazzle one another so as to harmonize their hearts;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant wishes to set institutions for the people to guard against excess, so that poor and rich do not dazzle one another and their hearts may be harmonized;

sentences.zh: 心志定，則盜賊消，刑罰少，陰陽和，萬物蕃也。

translations.literal: when hearts and wills are settled, then bandits and robbers vanish, punishments are few, yin and yang harmonize, and the ten thousand things flourish.
translations.idiomatic: when hearts and wills are settled, bandits vanish, punishments grow few, yin and yang harmonize, and the ten thousand things flourish.

sentences.zh: 昔秦王意廣心逸，欲威海外，使蒙恬將兵以北攻胡，又使尉屠睢將樓船之士以攻越。

translations.literal: Formerly the King of Qin's intent was broad and his heart at ease; he wished to awe the lands beyond the sea, sent Meng Tian to lead troops north to attack the Hu, and also sent Commandant Tu Sui to lead tower-ship soldiers to attack Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the King of Qin's ambitions were broad and his heart restless; he wished to awe the lands beyond the sea, sent Meng Tian with troops north against the Hu, and also sent Commandant Tu Sui with tower-ship troops against Yue.

sentences.zh: 當是時，秦禍北構於胡，南掛於越，宿兵於無用之地，進而不得退。

translations.literal: At that time Qin's calamity was built in the north with the Hu, hung in the south on Yue, quartered troops in useless places, advanced yet could not retreat.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qin's calamity was built in the north with the Hu and hung in the south on Yue; troops were quartered in useless places, advanced yet could not retreat.

sentences.zh: 行十餘年，丁男被甲，丁女轉輸，苦不聊生；

translations.literal: For more than ten years adult males donned armor, adult females hauled supplies, suffering without means to live;
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years adult males donned armor and adult females hauled supplies, suffering beyond endurance;

sentences.zh: 自經於道樹，死者相望。

translations.literal: they hanged themselves on roadside trees; the dead faced one another.
translations.idiomatic: men hanged themselves on roadside trees; the dead lined the roads.

sentences.zh: 及秦皇帝崩，天下大畔，滅世絕祀，窮兵之禍也。

translations.literal: When the First Emperor of Qin died, all under Heaven greatly turned away; lines were extinguished and sacrifices cut off—the calamity of exhausting arms.
translations.idiomatic: When the First Emperor of Qin died, all under Heaven rose in revolt; dynasties were extinguished and sacrifices ended—the calamity of exhausting arms.

sentences.zh: 故周失之弱，秦失之強，不變之患也。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhou failed through weakness, Qin failed through strength—the affliction of not changing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou failed through weakness, Qin through strength—the affliction of failing to change course.

sentences.zh: 今徇西夷，朝夜郎，降羌、僰，略薉州，建城邑，深入匈奴，燔其龍城，議者美之。

translations.literal: Now to drive the western Yi, have Yelang attend court, subdue Qiang and Bo, overrun Mizhou, build cities and towns, penetrate deep into the Xiongnu, and burn their Dragon City—deliberators praise it.
translations.idiomatic: Now we drive the western Yi, have Yelang attend court, subdue the Qiang and Bo, overrun Mizhou, build cities and towns, penetrate deep into the Xiongnu, and burn their Dragon City—counselors praise this.

sentences.zh: 此人臣之利，非天下之長策也。

translations.literal: This is the profit of ministers and subjects, not the long-term policy of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: This is profit for ministers and subjects, not the long-term policy of the realm.

sentences.zh: 徐樂上書曰：

translations.literal: Xu Le submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xu Le submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: :「臣聞天下之患，在於土崩，不在瓦解，古今一也。

translations.literal: : "Your servant hears that the affliction of all under Heaven lies in earthen collapse, not in tile disintegration—the same in antiquity and today.
translations.idiomatic: : "Your servant hears that the affliction of all under Heaven lies in earthen collapse, not in tile disintegration—the same in antiquity and today.

sentences.zh: :「何謂土崩？

translations.literal: : "What is called earthen collapse?
translations.idiomatic: : "What is earthen collapse?

sentences.zh: 秦之末世是也。

translations.literal: The last age of Qin was such.
translations.idiomatic: The last age of Qin was such.

sentences.zh: 陳涉無千乘之尊、疆土之地，身非王公、大人、名族之後，鄉曲之譽，非有孔、曾、墨子之賢，陶朱、猗頓之富也；

translations.literal: Chen She had no honor of a thousand chariots or territory of a thousand li; his person was not after kings, dukes, great men, or famous clans, nor village praise; he did not have the worth of Confucius, Zengzi, or Mozi, nor the wealth of Tao Zhu or Yi Dun;
translations.idiomatic: Chen She had neither the honor of a thousand chariots nor a thousand li of territory; he was no descendant of kings, dukes, great men, or famous clans, nor had he village renown; he lacked the worth of Confucius, Zengzi, or Mozi, or the wealth of Tao Zhu or Yi Dun;

sentences.zh: 然起窮巷，奮棘矜，偏袒大呼，天下從風。

translations.literal: yet he rose from a poor lane, brandished a thorn staff, bared one shoulder and shouted greatly, and all under Heaven followed like wind.
translations.idiomatic: yet he rose from a poor lane, seized a thorn staff, bared his shoulder and shouted, and all under Heaven followed like wind.

sentences.zh: 此其故何也？

translations.literal: What was the reason for this?
translations.idiomatic: Why was this so?

sentences.zh: 由民困而主不恤，下怨而上不知，俗已亂而政不修。

translations.literal: Because the people were distressed yet the ruler did not comfort them; below there was resentment yet above there was no knowledge; custom was already in disorder yet government was not repaired.
translations.idiomatic: Because the people were distressed yet the ruler did not comfort them; below there was resentment yet above there was no knowledge; custom was already in disorder yet government was not repaired.

sentences.zh: 此三者，陳涉之所以為資也，此之謂土崩。

translations.literal: These three were what Chen She took as his resources—this is what is called earthen collapse.
translations.idiomatic: These three were what Chen She drew upon—this is what is called earthen collapse.

sentences.zh: 故曰天下之患在乎土崩。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said the affliction of all under Heaven lies in earthen collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said the affliction of all under Heaven lies in earthen collapse.

sentences.zh: :「何謂瓦解？

translations.literal: : "What is called tile disintegration?
translations.idiomatic: : "What is tile disintegration?

sentences.zh: 吳、楚、齊、趙之兵是也。

translations.literal: The troops of Wu, Chu, Qi, and Zhao were such.
translations.idiomatic: The troops of Wu, Chu, Qi, and Zhao were such.

sentences.zh: 七國謀為大逆，號皆稱萬乘之君，帶甲數十萬，威足以嚴其境內，財足以勸其士民；

translations.literal: The seven states plotted great treason; all styled themselves rulers of ten thousand chariots, bore armor in several hundred thousands, authority enough to make strict their borders within, wealth enough to encourage their knights and people;
translations.idiomatic: The seven states plotted great treason; all styled themselves rulers of ten thousand chariots, bore armor in the hundreds of thousands, had authority enough to enforce order within their borders and wealth enough to encourage their knights and people;

sentences.zh: 然不能西攘尺寸之地，而身為禽於中原者，此其故何也？

translations.literal: yet they could not westward seize even an inch of ground, and their persons were taken captive in the central plains—what was the reason for this?
translations.idiomatic: yet they could not seize even an inch of ground westward, and their persons were taken captive in the central plains—why was this?

sentences.zh: 非權輕於匹夫而兵弱於陳涉也。

translations.literal: It was not that their authority was lighter than a common man's or their troops weaker than Chen She's.
translations.idiomatic: It was not that their authority was lighter than a commoner's or their troops weaker than Chen She's.

sentences.zh: 當是之時，先帝之德未衰而安土樂俗之民眾，故諸侯無竟外之助，此之謂瓦解。

translations.literal: At that time the former emperor's virtue had not declined and the people who settled the soil and delighted in custom were numerous; therefore the feudal lords had no aid from beyond their borders—this is what is called tile disintegration.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the former emperor's virtue had not declined and the people who loved their soil and custom were numerous; therefore the feudal lords had no aid from beyond their borders—this is what is called tile disintegration.

sentences.zh: 故曰天下之患不在瓦解。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said the affliction of all under Heaven is not in tile disintegration.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said the affliction of all under Heaven is not in tile disintegration.

sentences.zh: :「此二體者，安危之明要，賢主之一留意而深察也。

translations.literal: : "These two forms are the clear essentials of security and peril; a worthy ruler should at once take note and examine deeply.
translations.idiomatic: : "These two forms are the clear essentials of security and peril; a worthy ruler should heed them and examine them deeply.

sentences.zh: :「間者，關東五穀數不登，年歲未復，民多窮困，重之以邊境之事，推數循理而觀之，民宜有不安其處者矣。

translations.literal: : "Recently in the lands east of the passes the five grains several times did not mature, years have not recovered, the people are mostly poor and distressed, and on top of this are border affairs—pushing numbers and following reason to observe it, the people ought already to have those not secure in their places.
translations.idiomatic: : "Recently east of the passes the five grains have several times failed, the years have not recovered, the people are mostly poor and distressed, and on top of this come border affairs—reasoning from the numbers, the people ought already to have those who cannot rest secure in their places.

sentences.zh: 不安，故易動；

translations.literal: Not secure, therefore easy to stir;
translations.idiomatic: Not secure, therefore easy to stir;

sentences.zh: 易動者，土崩之勢也。

translations.literal: easy to stir—that is the momentum of earthen collapse.
translations.idiomatic: easy to stir—that is the momentum of earthen collapse.

sentences.zh: 故賢主獨觀萬化之原，明於安危之機，修之廟堂之上而銷未形之患也，其要期使天下無土崩之勢而已矣。

translations.literal: Therefore a worthy ruler alone observes the origin of the ten thousand transformations, is clear on the pivot of security and peril, repairs it above in the ancestral temple hall and dissolves misfortune not yet formed; the essential is simply to expect to make all under Heaven without the momentum of earthen collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore a worthy ruler alone observes the source of the ten thousand transformations, is clear on the pivot of security and peril, repairs policy in the ancestral temple and dissolves misfortune not yet formed; the essential is simply to keep all under Heaven from the momentum of earthen collapse.

sentences.zh: 書奏，天子召見三人，謂曰：「公等皆安在，何相見之晚也！

translations.literal: When the memorials were submitted, the Son of Heaven summoned and met the three men, saying to them: "Where have you gentlemen all been—why is meeting you so late!
translations.idiomatic: When the memorials were submitted, the emperor summoned the three men and said to them, "Where have you gentlemen been—why did we meet so late!

sentences.zh: 」皆拜為郎中。

translations.literal: " All were appointed Gentlemen of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: " All were appointed Gentlemen of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 主父偃尤親幸，一歲中凡四遷，為中大夫。

translations.literal: Zhu Fu Yan was especially favored and intimate; within one year he was promoted four times in all and made Palace Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fu Yan was especially favored; within one year he was promoted four times in all and made Palace Grandee.

sentences.zh: 大臣畏其口，賂遺累千金。

translations.literal: Great ministers feared his mouth; bribes and gifts piled to a thousand jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers feared his tongue; bribes and gifts piled to a thousand jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 或謂偃曰：「太橫矣！

translations.literal: Someone said to Yan: "Too overbearing!
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Yan, "You are too overbearing!

sentences.zh: 」偃曰：「吾生不五鼎食，死即五鼎烹耳！

translations.literal: " Yan said: "In life I did not eat from five tripods; in death let me be boiled in five tripods!
translations.idiomatic: " Yan said, "In life I did not dine from five tripods; in death let me be boiled in five tripods!

sentences.zh: 1冬，賜淮南王-{几}-杖，毋朝。

translations.literal: 1 In winter, the Prince of Huainan was granted the staff of office and exemption from court attendance and told not to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In winter, the Prince of Huainan was granted the staff of office and exemption from court attendance and told not to attend court.

sentences.zh: ----2主父偃說上曰：「古者諸侯不過百里，強弱之形易制。

translations.literal: ----2 Zhu Fu Yan persuaded the emperor, saying: "In antiquity feudal lords did not exceed a hundred li; the form of strong and weak was easy to control.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 Zhu Fu Yan persuaded the emperor, saying, "In antiquity feudal lords did not exceed a hundred li; the balance of strong and weak was easy to control.

sentences.zh: 今諸侯或連城數十，地方千里，緩則驕奢，易為淫亂，急則阻其強而合從以逆京師。

translations.literal: Now feudal lords sometimes link cities in several tens, with territory of a thousand li; when relaxed they are arrogant and extravagant, easily given to lewd disorder; when pressed they block their strength and form horizontal alliances to oppose the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Now feudal lords sometimes link dozens of cities and hold a thousand li of territory; when relaxed they grow arrogant and extravagant and easily fall into disorder; when pressed they use their strength to form alliances against the capital.

sentences.zh: 以法割削之，則逆節萌起，前日晁錯是也。

translations.literal: To cut and pare them by law, then rebellious nodes sprout—Chao Cuo the other day was such.
translations.idiomatic: Cut them by law and rebellious nodes sprout—Chao Cuo the other day was the example.

sentences.zh: 今諸侯子弟或十數，而適嗣代立，餘雖骨肉，無尺地之封，則仁孝之道不宣。

translations.literal: Now feudal lords' sons and younger brothers may number a dozen or so, yet the legitimate heir alone succeeds and stands; the rest, though flesh and bone, have not a foot of land enfeoffed—then the Way of benevolence and filial piety is not displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Now a feudal lord's sons and younger brothers may number a dozen or more, yet only the legitimate heir succeeds; the rest, though kin, receive not a foot of land—then the Way of benevolence and filial piety is not displayed.

sentences.zh: 願陛下令諸侯得推恩分子弟，以地侯之，彼人人喜得所願。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to order that feudal lords may extend grace and divide among sons and younger brothers, enfeoffing them with land as marquises—each of them will delight in obtaining his wish.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to order that feudal lords may extend grace and divide land among sons and younger brothers, enfeoffing them as marquises—each will delight in obtaining his wish.

sentences.zh: 上以德施，實分其國，不削而稍弱矣。

translations.literal: Above, grace is applied by virtue; in fact their states are divided—without cutting and paring they are gradually weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Above, grace is applied by virtue; in fact their states are divided—without direct cutting they are gradually weakened.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor followed this.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，詔曰：「諸侯王或欲推私恩分子弟邑者，令各條上，朕且臨定其號名。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, an edict said: "Feudal kings who wish to extend private grace and divide fiefs among sons and younger brothers—let each list and submit upward; We shall presently settle their titles and names.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, an edict said, "Feudal kings who wish to extend private grace and divide fiefs among sons and younger brothers—let each submit a list; We shall presently settle their titles and names.

sentences.zh: 」於是籓國始分，而子弟畢侯矣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon feudal states first were divided, and sons and younger brothers were all enfeoffed as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon feudal states were first divided, and sons and younger brothers were all enfeoffed as marquises.

sentences.zh: ----3匈奴入上谷、漁陽，殺略吏民千餘人。

translations.literal: ----3 The Xiongnu entered Shanggu and Yuyang, killing and carrying off officials and people—more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 The Xiongnu entered Shanggu and Yuyang, killing and carrying off officials and people—more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 遣衛青、李息出雲中以西至隴西，擊胡之樓煩、白羊王於河南，得胡首虜數千，牛羊百餘萬，走白羊、樓煩王，遂取河南地。

translations.literal: He dispatched Wei Qing and Li Xi out from Yunzhong west to Longxi, striking the Xiongnu's Loufan and Baiyang kings at Henan, obtaining several thousand Xiongnu heads and captives and more than a million cattle and sheep; the Baiyang and Loufan kings fled, and they then took the Henan lands.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Wei Qing and Li Xi from Yunzhong west to Longxi, striking the Xiongnu's Loufan and Baiyang kings south of the river, taking several thousand heads and captives and more than a million cattle and sheep; the Baiyang and Loufan kings fled, and they then took the Henan lands.

sentences.zh: 詔封青為長平侯，青校尉蘇建、張次公皆有功，封建為平陵侯，次公為岸頭侯。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed Qing as Marquis of Changping; Qing's aides Su Jian and Zhang Cigong all had merit—Su Jian was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingling, Cigong as Marquis of Antou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict enfeoffed Qing as Marquis of Changping; Qing's aides Su Jian and Zhang Cigong all had merit—Su Jian was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingling, Cigong as Marquis of Antou.

sentences.zh: 主父偃言：「河南地肥饒，外阻河，蒙恬城之以逐匈奴，內省轉輸戍漕，廣中國，滅胡之本也。

translations.literal: Zhu Fu Yan said: "The Henan lands are rich and fertile, outwardly blocked by the river; Meng Tian walled them to drive off the Xiongnu, inwardly economizing relay transport, garrison grain supply, broadening the central lands—the root of extinguishing the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fu Yan said, "The Henan lands are rich and fertile, outwardly blocked by the river; Meng Tian walled them to drive off the Xiongnu, inwardly economizing relay transport and garrison supply, broadening the central lands—the root of extinguishing the Hu.

sentences.zh: 」上下公卿議，皆言不便。

translations.literal: " Above and below, dukes and ministers deliberated; all said it was not convenient.
translations.idiomatic: " The court deliberated above and below; all said it was impracticable.

sentences.zh: 上竟用偃計，立朔方郡，使蘇建興十餘萬人築朔方城，復繕故秦時蒙恬所為塞，因河為固。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end used Yan's plan, established Shuofang commandery, had Su Jian raise more than a hundred thousand men to build Shuofang city, again repair the barrier Meng Tian had made in Qin times, and take the river as fortification.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in the end used Yan's plan, established Shuofang commandery, had Su Jian raise more than a hundred thousand men to build Shuofang city, repair the barrier Meng Tian had made in Qin times, and take the river as fortification.

sentences.zh: 轉漕甚遠，自山東咸被其勞，費數十百巨萬，府庫並虛；

translations.literal: Grain transport by water was very far; from the lands east of the mountains all suffered its labor; costs ran to several tens and hundreds of great ten-thousands; treasuries together were emptied;
translations.idiomatic: Grain transport ran very far; from the lands east of the mountains all suffered the labor; costs ran to tens and hundreds of millions; the treasuries were emptied together;

sentences.zh: 漢亦棄上谷之斗辟縣造陽地以予胡。

translations.literal: Han also abandoned Shanggu's narrow frontier counties and the Zaoyang region to give to the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Han also abandoned Shanggu's narrow frontier counties and the Zaoyang region to give to the Hu.

sentences.zh: ----4三月，乙亥晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: ----4 In the third month, on yihai, the last day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In the third month, on yihai, the last day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: ----5夏，募民徙朔方十萬口。

translations.literal: ----5 In summer, the people were recruited to move a hundred thousand mouths to Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In summer, the people were recruited to move a hundred thousand mouths to Shuofang.

sentences.zh: ----6主父偃說上曰：「茂陵初立，天下豪桀，並兼之家，亂眾之民，皆可徙茂陵；

translations.literal: ----6 Zhu Fu Yan persuaded the emperor, saying: "Maoling was newly established; the realm's powerful heroes, households that merged and swallowed others, and people who stirred the masses—all may be moved to Maoling;
translations.idiomatic: ----6 Zhu Fu Yan persuaded the emperor, saying, "Maoling was newly established; the realm's powerful heroes, households that merged estates, and people who stirred the masses—all may be moved to Maoling;

sentences.zh: 內實京師，外銷奸猾，此所謂不誅而害除。

translations.literal: inwardly filling the capital region, outwardly dissolving treacherous and slippery men—this is what is called removing harm without executing.
translations.idiomatic: inwardly filling the capital region, outwardly dissolving the treacherous and slippery—this is what is called removing harm without executing.

sentences.zh: 」上從之，徙郡國豪傑及訾三百萬以上於茂陵。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this and moved powerful heroes of the commanderies and kingdoms and those with property of three million or more to Maoling.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor followed this and moved powerful heroes of the commanderies and kingdoms and those with property of three million or more to Maoling.

sentences.zh: 軹人郭解，關東大俠也，亦在徙中。

translations.literal: Guo Jie of Zhi, a great knight-errant of the lands east of the passes, was also among those to be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jie of Zhi, a great knight-errant east of the passes, was also among those to be moved.

sentences.zh: 衛將軍為言：「郭解家貧，不中徙。

translations.literal: The General-in-Chief spoke for him: "Guo Jie's family is poor—not fit for relocation.
translations.idiomatic: The General-in-Chief spoke for him: "Guo Jie's family is poor—not fit for relocation.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「解，布衣，權至使將軍為言，此其家不貧。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Jie is a plain-clothed man, yet his authority reaches the point of making a general speak for him—his family is not poor.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Jie is a commoner, yet his authority reaches the point of making a general speak for him—his family is not poor.

sentences.zh: 」卒徙解家。

translations.literal: " In the end Jie's family was moved.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end Jie's family was moved.

sentences.zh: 解平生睚眥殺人甚眾，上聞之，下吏捕治解，所殺皆在赦前。

translations.literal: Jie in his life for petty grudges killed very many; the emperor heard and sent officials down to seize and try Jie—the killings were all before amnesties.
translations.idiomatic: Jie in his life had killed many over petty grudges; the emperor heard and sent officials to seize and try him—the killings were all before amnesties.

sentences.zh: 軹有儒生侍使者坐，客譽郭解，生曰：「解專以奸犯公法，何謂賢！

translations.literal: In Zhi a Confucian scholar attended the envoy seated; a guest praised Guo Jie; the scholar said: "Jie specializes in wickedness that violates public law—how is he called worthy!
translations.idiomatic: In Zhi a Confucian scholar sat with the envoy; a guest praised Guo Jie; the scholar said, "Jie specializes in wickedness that violates public law—how is he called worthy!

sentences.zh: 」解客聞，殺此生，斷其舌。

translations.literal: " Jie's guest heard, killed this scholar, and cut off his tongue.
translations.idiomatic: " Jie's guest heard, killed the scholar, and cut off his tongue.

sentences.zh: 吏以此責解，解實不知殺者，殺者亦竟絕，莫知為誰。

translations.literal: Officials for this held Jie responsible; Jie truly did not know the killer; the killer also in the end was cut off—none knew who it was.
translations.idiomatic: Officials for this held Jie responsible; Jie truly did not know the killer; the killer also vanished entirely—none knew who it was.

sentences.zh: 吏奏解無罪，公孫弘議曰：「解，布衣，為任俠行權，以睚眥殺人。

translations.literal: Officials reported Jie without crime; Gongsun Hong deliberated, saying: "Jie, a plain-clothed man, practiced chivalry and exercised authority, killing people for petty grudges.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported Jie without crime; Gongsun Hong argued, "Jie, a commoner, practiced chivalry and exercised authority, killing people over petty grudges.

sentences.zh: 解雖弗知，此罪甚於解殺之。

translations.literal: Though Jie did not know, this crime is greater than Jie killing.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jie did not know, this crime is greater than if Jie had killed.

sentences.zh: 當大逆無道。

translations.literal: He should be guilty of great treason and impiety.
translations.idiomatic: He should be guilty of great treason and impiety.

sentences.zh: 」遂族郭解。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Jie's clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Jie's clan was exterminated.

sentences.zh: :班固曰：::古者天子建國，諸侯立家，自卿大夫以至於庶人，各有等差，是以民服事其上而下無覬覦。

translations.literal: : Ban Gu said: :: In antiquity the Son of Heaven established states, feudal lords established households; from ministers and grandees down to commoners each had grades and differences—thus the people served those above and below had no coveting gaze.
translations.idiomatic: : Ban Gu said: :: In antiquity the Son of Heaven established states and feudal lords established households; from ministers and grandees down to commoners each had grades and differences—thus the people served those above and below had no coveting gaze.

sentences.zh: 周室既微，禮樂、征伐自諸侯出。

translations.literal: When the house of Zhou was already slight, ritual and music and campaigns and punishments issued from the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: When the house of Zhou had declined, ritual and music and campaigns and punishments issued from the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 桓、文之後，大夫世權，陪臣執命。

translations.literal: After Huan and Wen, grandees held hereditary power and attendant ministers grasped commands.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan and Wen, grandees held hereditary power and attendant ministers grasped commands.

sentences.zh: 陵夷至於戰國，合從連衡，繇是列國公子，魏人信陵，趙有平原，齊有孟嘗，楚有春申，皆藉王公之勢，競為遊俠，雞鳴狗盜，無不賓禮。

translations.literal: Decline stretched down to the Warring States; horizontal and vertical alliances arose—thereupon the princes of the ranked states: Xinling of Wei, Pingyuan in Zhao, Lord Mengchang in Qi, Lord Chunshen in Chu—all borrowed kings' and dukes' power, vied as roaming knights, and whether cock-crow or dog-steal, none went without guest ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Decline stretched down to the Warring States; horizontal and vertical alliances arose—thereupon the princes of the ranked states: Xinling of Wei, Pingyuan in Zhao, Lord Mengchang in Qi, Lord Chunshen in Chu—all borrowed royal and ducal power, vied as roaming knights, and whether cock-crow trick or dog-steal, none went without honored guest treatment.

sentences.zh: 而趙相虞卿，棄國捐君，以周窮交魏齊之厄；

translations.literal: Yet Zhao's chancellor Lord Yu, abandoning state and casting off his ruler, to circle and relieve the straits of his friend Lord Weiqi;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhao's chancellor Lord Yu, abandoning state and casting off his ruler, to relieve the straits of his friend Lord Weiqi;

sentences.zh: 信陵無忌，竊符矯命，戮將專師，以赴平原之急；

translations.literal: Xinling Wuji stole the tally and forged orders, killed a general and monopolized the army, to rush to Pingyuan's urgency;
translations.idiomatic: Xinling Wuji stole the tally and forged orders, killed a general and took sole command of the army, to rush to Pingyuan's urgency;

sentences.zh: 皆以取重諸侯，顯名天下，扼腕而游談者，以四豪為稱首。

translations.literal: all by these means gained weight among feudal lords and displayed fame under Heaven; those who clenched wrists and roamed in talk took the Four Heroes as their chief title.
translations.idiomatic: all by these means gained weight among feudal lords and displayed fame under Heaven; those who clenched wrists and roamed in talk took the Four Heroes as their chief title.

sentences.zh: 於是背公死黨之議成，守職奉上之義廢矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon discourse of turning the back on the public and dying for factions was formed, and the righteousness of keeping office and serving above was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon discourse of turning the back on the public and dying for factions took shape, and the righteousness of keeping office and serving above was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 及至漢興，禁網疏闊，未知匡改也。

translations.literal: When it reached Han's rise, the prohibitory net was loose and wide, and correction was not yet known.
translations.idiomatic: When Han arose, the prohibitory net was loose and wide, and correction was not yet known.

sentences.zh: 是故代相陳豨從車千乘，而吳濞、淮南皆招客以千數。

translations.literal: Therefore the Chancellor of Dai Chen Xi had a following of a thousand chariots, while Liu Pi of Wu and Huainan all recruited guests by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Chancellor of Dai Chen Xi had a following of a thousand chariots, while Liu Pi of Wu and Huainan all recruited guests by the thousands.

sentences.zh: 外戚大臣魏其、武安之屬競逐於京師，布衣遊俠劇孟、郭解之徒馳騖於閻閭、權行州域。

translations.literal: Affinal great ministers like Dou Ying and Tian Fen vied in pursuit at the capital; plain-clothed roaming knights like Ju Meng and Guo Jie raced through lanes and alleys, authority running through commandery domains.
translations.idiomatic: Affinal great ministers like Dou Ying and Tian Fen vied at the capital; plain-clothed roaming knights like Ju Meng and Guo Jie raced through lanes and alleys, their authority running through commandery domains.

sentences.zh: 力折公侯，眾庶榮其名跡，覬而慕之。

translations.literal: By force they bent down marquises and earls; the masses gloried their names and traces, coveting and admiring them.
translations.idiomatic: By force they bent down marquises and earls; the masses gloried their names and deeds, coveting and admiring them.

sentences.zh: 雖其陷於刑辟，自與殺身成名，若季路、仇牧，死而不悔。

translations.literal: Though they fell into penal law, they themselves paired killing the body with completing fame, like Zilu and Qiu Mu—dying without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Though they fell under penal law, they themselves paired death with completed fame, like Zilu and Qiu Mu—dying without regret.

sentences.zh: 故曾子曰：「上失其道，民散久矣。

translations.literal: Therefore Zengzi said: "When above loses the Way, the people have been scattered long.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Zengzi said, "When above loses the Way, the people have been scattered long.

sentences.zh: 」非明王在上，示之以好惡，齊之以禮法，民曷由知禁而反正乎！

translations.literal: " Without a bright king above to show them likes and dislikes and align them with ritual and law, how could the people know prohibition and return to the correct!
translations.idiomatic: " Without a bright king above to show them likes and dislikes and align them with ritual and law, how could the people know prohibition and return to the correct!

sentences.zh: 古之正法：五伯，三王之罪人也；

translations.literal: The correct law of antiquity: the Five Hegemons were criminals of the Three Kings;
translations.idiomatic: The correct law of antiquity: the Five Hegemons were criminals of the Three Kings;

sentences.zh: 而六國，五伯之罪人也。

translations.literal: and the six states were criminals of the Five Hegemons.
translations.idiomatic: and the six states were criminals of the Five Hegemons.

sentences.zh: 夫四豪者，又六國之罪人也。

translations.literal: The Four Heroes, moreover, were also criminals of the six states.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Heroes, moreover, were also criminals of the six states.

sentences.zh: 況於郭解之倫，以匹夫之細，竊殺生之權，其罪已不容於誅矣。

translations.literal: How much more for men like Guo Jie—by the minuteness of a common fellow, stealthily usurping the power over life and death; their crime already cannot be contained within execution.
translations.idiomatic: How much more so for men like Guo Jie—mere commoners who stealthily usurped the power of life and death; their crimes already exceeded what execution could contain.

sentences.zh: 觀其溫良泛愛，振窮周急，謙退不伐，亦皆有絕異之姿。

translations.literal: Observing their gentleness and kindness, broad love, rousing the poor and relieving the urgent, humility and retreat without boasting—they all also had postures of surpassing strangeness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet observing their gentleness and broad compassion, their relief of the poor and aid to the distressed, their humility without boasting—they all had qualities of surpassing distinction.

sentences.zh: 惜乎，不入於道德，苟放縱於末流，殺身亡宗，非不幸也。

translations.literal: Alas, not entering into virtue and the Way, recklessly indulging in the lower current—body killed and clan extinguished; this is not misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, they did not enter the Way of virtue but recklessly indulged the lower current; death and the extinction of their clans were not misfortune.

sentences.zh: :荀悅論曰：::世有三游，德之賊也：一曰遊俠，二曰遊說，三曰遊行。

translations.literal: : Xun Yue remarked, saying: :: In the world there are three wanderings, thieves of virtue: first, roaming knights; second, roaming persuaders; third, roaming conduct.
translations.idiomatic: : Xun Yue remarked: :: In the world there are three wanderings, thieves of virtue: first, roaming knights; second, roaming persuaders; third, roaming conduct.

sentences.zh: 立氣勢，作威福，結私交以立強於世者，謂之遊俠；

translations.literal: Establishing vital momentum, making authority and blessing, knotting private ties to stand strong in the age—this is called roaming knights;
translations.idiomatic: those who build up vital momentum, wield authority and favor, and knot private ties to stand strong in the world are called roaming knights;

sentences.zh: 飾辯辭，設詐謀，馳逐於天下以要時勢者，謂之遊說；

translations.literal: adorning disputatious words, setting deceitful schemes, racing and chasing through all under Heaven to seize the timely momentum—this is called roaming persuasion;
translations.idiomatic: those who adorn disputatious words, set deceitful schemes, and race through all under Heaven to seize the timely momentum are called roaming persuaders;

sentences.zh: 色取仁以合時好，連黨類，立虛譽以為權利者，謂之遊行。

translations.literal: taking on the color of benevolence to match the age's likes, linking factional kinds, establishing empty fame to serve as authority and profit—this is called roaming conduct.
translations.idiomatic: those who take on the color of benevolence to match the age's tastes, link factions, and establish empty fame for authority and profit are called roaming conduct.

sentences.zh: 此三者，亂之所由生也；

translations.literal: These three are what disorder is born from;
translations.idiomatic: these three are what disorder is born from;

sentences.zh: 傷道害德，敗法惑世，先王之所慎也。

translations.literal: injuring the Way and harming virtue, defeating law and bewildering the age—what former kings were cautious of.
translations.idiomatic: they injure the Way and harm virtue, defeat law and bewilder the age—what former kings were cautious of.

sentences.zh: 國有四民，各修其業。

translations.literal: The state has four peoples, each cultivating his calling.
translations.idiomatic: The state has four peoples, each cultivating his calling.

sentences.zh: 不由四民之業者，謂之奸民。

translations.literal: Those who do not follow the callings of the four peoples are called treacherous people.
translations.idiomatic: Those who do not follow the callings of the four peoples are called treacherous people.

sentences.zh: 奸民不生，王道乃成。

translations.literal: When treacherous people are not born, the kingly Way is then accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: When treacherous people do not arise, the kingly Way is accomplished.

sentences.zh: ::凡此三游之作，生於季世，周、秦之末尤甚焉。

translations.literal: :: All these three wanderings' arising was born in the late age; at the ends of Zhou and Qin they were especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: :: All these three wanderings arose in the late age; at the ends of Zhou and Qin they were especially severe.

sentences.zh: 上不明，下不正，制度不立，綱紀馳廢；

translations.literal: Above was not bright, below was not correct, institutions were not established, cords and threads were slack and abandoned;
translations.idiomatic: above was not bright, below was not correct, institutions were not established, and discipline was slack and abandoned;

sentences.zh: 以毀譽為榮辱，不核其真；

translations.literal: taking slander and praise as honor and disgrace, not examining their truth;
translations.idiomatic: slander and praise were taken as honor and disgrace without examining their truth;

sentences.zh: 以愛憎為利害，不論其實；

translations.literal: taking love and hate as benefit and harm, not deliberating their reality;
translations.idiomatic: love and hate were taken as benefit and harm without deliberating the facts;

sentences.zh: 以喜怒為賞罰，不察其理。

translations.literal: taking joy and anger as reward and punishment, not discerning their principle.
translations.idiomatic: joy and anger were taken as reward and punishment without discerning principle.

sentences.zh: 上下相冒，萬事乖錯，是以言論者計薄厚而吐辭，選舉者度親疏而舉筆，善惡謬於眾聲，功罪亂於王法。

translations.literal: Above and below mutually encroached; the ten thousand affairs were perverse and wrong—thus speakers calculated thickness and thinness in spitting forth words, selectors measured near and far in lifting the brush; good and evil were mistaken by the crowd's voices, merit and crime were confused in the king's law.
translations.idiomatic: above and below encroached on one another; the ten thousand affairs went awry—thus speakers weighed gain in their words, selectors measured kinship in their choices; good and evil were mistaken by public clamor, merit and crime confused in royal law.

sentences.zh: 然則利不可以義求，害不可以道避也。

translations.literal: Then profit could not be sought by righteousness, harm could not be avoided by the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Then profit could not be sought by righteousness, nor harm avoided by the Way.

sentences.zh: 是以君子犯禮，小人犯法，奔走馳騁，越職僭度，飾華廢實，競趣時利。

translations.literal: Therefore gentlemen violated ritual, petty men violated law; running and racing, overstepping offices and transgressing measures, adorning the florid and abandoning the real, competing toward timely profit.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore gentlemen violated ritual and petty men violated law; all raced about, overstepping office and transgressing bounds, adorning show and abandoning substance, competing for timely profit.

sentences.zh: 簡父兄之尊而崇賓客之禮，薄骨肉之恩而篤朋友之愛，忘修身之道而求眾人之譽，割衣食之業以供饗宴之好，苞苴盈於門庭，聘問交於道路，書記繁於公文，私務眾於官事，於是流俗成而正道壞矣。

translations.literal: They made light of father and elder brothers' honor yet exalted guests' ritual, made thin flesh-and-bone kindness yet made thick friends' love, forgot the Way of cultivating the self yet sought the crowd's praise, cut off clothing and food callings to supply feasting and banqueting delights; bribes filled the gate and court, courtesy visits crossed on the roads, written records multiplied on public documents, private affairs outnumbered official business—thereupon vulgar custom formed and the correct Way was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: They slighted the honor due fathers and elder brothers yet exalted guests' ritual, made thin the kindness owed kin yet made thick friends' love, forgot self-cultivation yet sought public praise, cut off livelihoods to supply feasting delights; bribes filled gate and court, courtesy visits crossed the roads, written records multiplied on public documents, private affairs outnumbered official business—thereupon vulgar custom formed and the correct Way was ruined.

sentences.zh: ::是以聖王在上，經國序民，正其制度；

translations.literal: :: Therefore when a sage king is above, he threads the state and orders the people, rectifying his institutions;
translations.idiomatic: :: Therefore when a sage king is above, he governs the state and orders the people, rectifying institutions;

sentences.zh: 善惡要於功罪而不淫於毀譽，聽其言而責其事，舉其名而指其實。

translations.literal: good and evil hinge on merit and crime and do not overflow into slander and praise; he hears their words and holds them to their affairs, lifts their names and points to their reality.
translations.idiomatic: good and evil hinge on merit and crime and do not overflow into slander and praise; he hears their words and holds them to their deeds, lifts their names and points to their reality.

sentences.zh: 故實不應其聲者謂之虛，情不覆其貌者謂之偽，毀譽失其真者謂之誣，言事失其類者謂之罔。

translations.literal: Therefore reality not answering its sound is called empty; feeling not covering its appearance is called false; slander and praise losing their truth is called deceit; words and affairs losing their kind is called confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore reality that does not answer its sound is called empty; feeling that does not match appearance is called false; slander and praise that lose truth are called deceit; words and affairs that miss their kind are called confusion.

sentences.zh: 虛偽之行不得設，誣罔之辭不得行，有罪惡者無僥倖，無罪過者不憂懼，請謁無所行，貨賂無所用，息華文，去浮辭，禁偽辯，絕淫智，放百家之紛亂，壹聖人之至道，養之以仁惠，文之以禮樂，則風俗定而大化成矣。

translations.literal: Empty and false conduct cannot be set up; deceitful and confused words cannot be carried out; those with crime and evil have no lucky escape, those without fault or error have no worry or fear; private requests have nowhere to go, goods-bribes have no use; florid writing is stilled, floating words removed, false disputation forbidden, excessive cleverness cut off; the hundred schools' confusion is released, the sage's utmost Way is made one; nourished by benevolence and grace, patterned by ritual and music—then custom is settled and great transformation is accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Empty and false conduct cannot stand; deceitful words cannot prevail; the guilty have no lucky escape, the innocent have no fear; private requests go nowhere, bribes avail nothing; florid writing is stilled, floating words removed, false disputation forbidden, excessive cleverness cut off; the hundred schools' confusion is set aside and the sage's utmost Way made one; nourished by benevolence and grace, patterned by ritual and music—then custom is settled and great transformation is accomplished.

sentences.zh: ----7燕王定國與父康王姬奸，奪弟妻為姬，殺肥如令郢人。

translations.literal: ----7 The Prince of Yan Dingguo committed incest with his father King Kang's concubine, seized his younger brother's wife as a concubine, and killed Feiru magistrate Ying Ren.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 The Prince of Yan Dingguo committed incest with his father King Kang's concubine, seized his younger brother's wife as a concubine, and killed Feiru magistrate Ying Ren.

sentences.zh: 郢人兄弟上書告之，主父偃從中發其事。

translations.literal: Ying Ren's brothers submitted a memorial accusing him; Zhu Fu Yan from within exposed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Ren's brothers submitted a memorial accusing him; Zhu Fu Yan exposed the affair from within.

sentences.zh: 公卿請誅定國，上許之。

translations.literal: Dukes and ministers requested executing Dingguo; the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and ministers requested that Dingguo be executed; the emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 定國自殺，國除。

translations.literal: Dingguo killed himself; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo killed himself; the state was abolished.

sentences.zh: 齊厲王次昌亦與其姊紀翁主通。

translations.literal: Qi Licheng King Cichang also had relations with his elder sister Princess Ji Wengzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Licheng King Cichang also had relations with his elder sister Princess Ji Wengzhu.

sentences.zh: 主父偃欲納其女於齊王，齊紀太后不許。

translations.literal: Zhu Fu Yan wished to marry his daughter to the King of Qi; the Qi Ji Empress Dowager did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fu Yan wished to marry his daughter to the King of Qi; the Qi Ji Empress Dowager did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 偃因言於上曰：「齊臨菑十萬戶，市租千金，人眾殷富，巨於長安，非天子親弟、愛子，不得王此。

translations.literal: Yan therefore spoke to the emperor, saying: "Qi at Linzi has a hundred thousand households; market rents are a thousand jin of gold; the people are numerous, prosperous, and rich—greater than Chang'an. Unless the Son of Heaven's close younger brother or beloved son, one may not be king here.
translations.idiomatic: Yan therefore said to the emperor, "Qi at Linzi has a hundred thousand households; market rents are a thousand jin of gold; the people are numerous, prosperous, and rich—greater than Chang'an. Only the emperor's close younger brother or beloved son should be king here.

sentences.zh: 今齊王於親屬益疏，又聞與其姊亂，請治之！

translations.literal: Now the King of Qi grows ever more distant among kin, and I have also heard of disorder with his elder sister—please try him!
translations.idiomatic: Now the King of Qi grows ever more distant among kin, and I have also heard of incest with his elder sister—please try him!

sentences.zh: 」於是帝拜偃為齊相，且正其事。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the emperor appointed Yan as Chancellor of Qi and also to rectify the affair.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the emperor appointed Yan as Chancellor of Qi and also to rectify the affair.

sentences.zh: 偃至齊，急治王后宮宦者，辭及王；

translations.literal: When Yan arrived in Qi, he urgently tried the queen's palace eunuchs; their testimony reached the king;
translations.idiomatic: When Yan arrived in Qi, he urgently tried the queen's palace eunuchs; their testimony implicated the king;

sentences.zh: 王懼，飲藥自殺。

translations.literal: the king feared and drank poison, killing himself.
translations.idiomatic: the king feared and drank poison, killing himself.

sentences.zh: 偃少時游齊及燕、趙，及貴，連敗燕、齊。

translations.literal: Yan in his youth wandered in Qi and also Yan and Zhao; when he became noble, he in succession brought down Yan and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan in his youth had wandered in Qi and also Yan and Zhao; when he rose to power, he in succession brought down Yan and Qi.

sentences.zh: 趙王彭祖懼，上書告主父偃受諸侯金，以故諸侯子弟多以得封者。

translations.literal: The King of Zhao Pengzu feared and submitted a memorial accusing Zhu Fu Yan of receiving gold from feudal lords—on that account many feudal lords' sons and younger brothers had obtained enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Zhao Pengzu feared and submitted a memorial accusing Zhu Fu Yan of receiving gold from feudal lords—on that account many feudal lords' sons and younger brothers had obtained enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 及齊王自殺，上聞，大怒，以為偃劫其王令自殺，乃征下吏。

translations.literal: When the King of Qi killed himself, the emperor heard and was greatly angry, thinking Yan had coerced his king to order self-death; he then summoned and sent him down to officials.
translations.idiomatic: When the King of Qi killed himself, the emperor heard and was greatly angry, thinking Yan had coerced the king into suicide; he then summoned him and sent him down to the officials.

sentences.zh: 偃服受諸侯金，實不劫王令自殺。

translations.literal: Yan confessed receiving feudal lords' gold; in fact he had not coerced the king to order self-death.
translations.idiomatic: Yan confessed receiving feudal lords' gold; in fact he had not coerced the king into suicide.

sentences.zh: 上欲勿誅，公孫弘曰：「齊王自殺，無後，國除為郡入漢，主父偃本首惡。

translations.literal: The emperor wished not to execute him; Gongsun Hong said: "The King of Qi killed himself, without posterity; the state was abolished and made a commandery entering Han—Zhu Fu Yan was originally the chief evil.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished not to execute him; Gongsun Hong said, "The King of Qi killed himself without posterity; the state was abolished and made a commandery of Han—Zhu Fu Yan was originally the chief culprit.

sentences.zh: 陛下不誅偃，無以謝天下。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not execute Yan, there is no means to apologize to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not execute Yan, there is no way to answer to all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」乃遂族主父偃。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he exterminated Zhu Fu Yan's clan.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he exterminated Zhu Fu Yan's clan.

sentences.zh: ----8張歐免，上欲以蓼侯孔臧為御史大夫。

translations.literal: ----8 Zhang Ou was dismissed; the emperor wished to make Marquis of Liao Kong Zang Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 Zhang Ou was dismissed; the emperor wished to make Marquis of Liao Kong Zang Grand Censor.

sentences.zh: 臧辭曰：「臣世以經學為業，乞為太常，典臣家業，與從弟侍中安國綱紀古訓，使永垂來嗣。

translations.literal: Zang declined, saying: "Your servant's family for generations has taken classical learning as its calling; I beg to be Grand Master of Ceremonies, overseeing my family's calling, together with my younger cousin from the father's clan, Palace Attendant Anguo, to thread and regulate ancient instruction, so that it may forever hang down to coming heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Zang declined, saying, "Your servant's family for generations has taken classical learning as its calling; I beg to be Grand Master of Ceremonies, overseeing my family's calling, together with my younger cousin from the father's clan, Palace Attendant Anguo, to preserve ancient instruction so that it may forever endure for coming heirs.

sentences.zh: 」上乃以臧為太常，其禮賜如三公。

translations.literal: " The emperor then made Zang Grand Master of Ceremonies; his ritual gifts were like the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then made Zang Grand Master of Ceremonies; his ritual gifts were like those of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 1冬，匈奴軍臣單于死，其弟左谷蠡王伊稚斜自立為單于，攻破軍臣單于太子於單，於單亡降漢。

translations.literal: 1 In winter, the Xiongnu Chanyu Junchen died; his younger brother, the Left Guli King Yizhixie, installed himself as Chanyu, defeated Chanyu Junchen's heir Yu Shan at Yu Shan, and Yu Shan fled and surrendered to Han.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In winter, the Xiongnu Chanyu Junchen died; his younger brother, the Left Guli King Yizhixie, installed himself as Chanyu, defeated Chanyu Junchen's heir Yu Shan at Yu Shan, and Yu Shan fled and surrendered to Han.

sentences.zh: ----2以公孫弘為御史大夫。

translations.literal: ----2 Gongsun Hong was made Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 Gongsun Hong was made Grand Censor.

sentences.zh: 是時，方通西南夷，東置蒼海，北築朔方之郡。

translations.literal: At this time, they were just opening communications with the southwestern Yi, establishing Canghai in the east, and building the Shuofang commandery in the north.
translations.idiomatic: At this time they were opening communications with the southwestern Yi, establishing Canghai in the east, and building the Shuofang commandery in the north.

sentences.zh: 公孫弘數諫，以為罷敝中國以奉無用之地，願罷之。

translations.literal: Gongsun Hong several times remonstrated, holding that they were exhausting and wearing out the central lands to supply useless territory, and wished to abandon it.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Hong several times remonstrated, holding that they were exhausting the central lands to supply useless territory, and wished to abandon these projects.

sentences.zh: 天子使朱買臣等難以置朔方之便；

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven had Zhu Maichen and others dispute the convenience of establishing Shuofang;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Zhu Maichen and others dispute the convenience of establishing Shuofang;

sentences.zh: 發十策，弘不得一。

translations.literal: they posed ten questions; Hong could not answer one.
translations.idiomatic: they posed ten questions; Hong could not answer one.

sentences.zh: 弘乃謝曰：「山東鄙人，不知其便若是，願罷西南夷、蒼海而專奉朔方。

translations.literal: Hong then apologized, saying: "A rustic fellow east of the mountains—I did not know its convenience was like this; I wish to abandon the southwestern Yi and Canghai and devote support solely to Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: Hong then apologized, saying, "A rustic fellow east of the mountains—I did not know its convenience was like this; I wish to abandon the southwestern Yi and Canghai and devote support solely to Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 」上乃許之，春，罷蒼海郡。

translations.literal: " The emperor then assented; in spring, Canghai commandery was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then assented; in spring, Canghai commandery was abolished.

sentences.zh: 弘為布被，食不重肉。

translations.literal: Hong used a hempen quilt and did not eat two kinds of meat at one meal.
translations.idiomatic: Hong used a hempen quilt and did not eat two kinds of meat at one meal.

sentences.zh: 汲黯曰：「弘位在三公，奉祿甚多；

translations.literal: Ji An said: "Hong's position is among the Three Excellencies; his salary and emoluments are very many;
translations.idiomatic: Ji An said, "Hong's position is among the Three Excellencies; his salary and emoluments are very great;

sentences.zh: 然為布被，此詐也。

translations.literal: yet he uses a hempen quilt—this is fraud.
translations.idiomatic: yet he uses a hempen quilt—this is fraud.

sentences.zh: 」上問弘，弘謝曰：「有之。

translations.literal: " The emperor questioned Hong; Hong apologized, saying: "It is so.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor questioned Hong; Hong apologized, saying, "It is so.

sentences.zh: 夫九卿臣善者無過黯，然今日廷詰弘，誠中弘之病。

translations.literal: Of the Nine Ministers' subjects who are good, none surpasses An; yet today in court he interrogated Hong—truly it struck Hong's ailment.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Nine Ministers' subjects who are good, none surpasses An; yet today in court he interrogated Hong—truly he struck Hong's fault.

sentences.zh: 夫以三公為布被，與小吏無差，誠飾詐，欲以釣名，如汲黯言。

translations.literal: For one of the Three Excellencies to use a hempen quilt, no different from petty clerks—truly adorning fraud, wishing thereby to fish for fame, as Ji An said.
translations.idiomatic: For one of the Three Excellencies to use a hempen quilt, no different from petty clerks—truly adorning fraud, wishing thereby to fish for fame, as Ji An said.

sentences.zh: 且無汲黯忠，陛下安得聞此言！

translations.literal: Moreover, without Ji An's loyalty, how would Your Majesty have heard these words!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, without Ji An's loyalty, how would Your Majesty have heard these words!

sentences.zh: 」天子以為謙讓，愈益厚之。

translations.literal: " The Son of Heaven considered this modest yielding and all the more treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor considered this modest yielding and all the more treated him generously.

sentences.zh: ----3三月，赦天下。

translations.literal: ----3 In the third month, there was an amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In the third month, there was an amnesty for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: ----4夏，四月，丙子，封匈奴太子於單為涉安侯，數月而卒。

translations.literal: ----4 In summer, the fourth month, on bingzi, the Xiongnu heir Yu Shan was enfeoffed as Marquis of She'an; after several months he died.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In summer, the fourth month, on bingzi, the Xiongnu heir Yu Shan was enfeoffed as Marquis of She'an; after several months he died.

sentences.zh: ----5初，匈奴降者言：「月氏故居敦煌、祁連間，為強國，匈奴冒頓攻破之。

translations.literal: ----5 Initially, a Xiongnu who had surrendered said: "The Yuezhi formerly dwelt between Dunhuang and Qilian, a strong state; the Xiongnu Modun broke and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 Initially, a Xiongnu who had surrendered said, "The Yuezhi formerly dwelt between Dunhuang and Qilian as a strong state; the Xiongnu Modun broke and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 老上單于殺月氏王，以其頭為飲器。

translations.literal: The Laoshang Chanyu killed the King of Yue, using his head as a drinking vessel.
translations.idiomatic: The Laoshang Chanyu killed the King of Yue, using his head as a drinking vessel.

sentences.zh: 餘眾遁逃遠去，怨匈奴，無與共擊之。

translations.literal: The remaining multitude fled far away, resenting the Xiongnu, and would not join in striking them.
translations.idiomatic: The remnant multitude fled far away, resenting the Xiongnu, and would not join in striking them.

sentences.zh: 」上募能通使月氏者，漢中張騫以郎應募，出隴西，逕匈奴中；

translations.literal: " The emperor recruited one able to go as envoy and communicate with the Yuezhi; Zhang Qian of Hanzhong, as a Gentleman, answered the recruitment, went out from Longxi, and went straight through the Xiongnu lands;
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor recruited one able to go as envoy to the Yuezhi; Zhang Qian of Hanzhong, as a Gentleman, answered the recruitment, went out from Longxi, and went straight through the Xiongnu lands;

sentences.zh: 單于得之，留騫十餘歲。

translations.literal: the Chanyu obtained him and detained Qian for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: the Chanyu seized him and detained Qian for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 騫得間亡，嚮月氏西走，數十日，至大宛。

translations.literal: Qian found an interval and fled, turning west toward the Yuezhi; after several tens of days he reached Great Fergana.
translations.idiomatic: Qian found an opening and fled, turning west toward the Yuezhi; after several tens of days he reached Great Fergana.

sentences.zh: 大宛聞漢之饒財，欲通不得，見騫，喜，為發導譯抵康居，傳致大月氏。

translations.literal: Great Fergana had heard that Han was rich in wealth and wished to communicate but could not; seeing Qian, they rejoiced, sent guides and interpreters to reach Kangju, and relayed him to Great Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: Great Fergana had heard that Han was rich in wealth and wished to communicate but could not; seeing Qian, they rejoiced, sent guides and interpreters to reach Kangju, and relayed him to Great Yuezhi.

sentences.zh: 大月氏太子為王，既擊大夏，分其地而居之，地肥饒，少寇，殊無報胡之心。

translations.literal: The Great Yuezhi heir had become king; having already struck Great Bactria, they divided its lands and dwelt there; the land was rich and fertile, with few raids, and utterly without a mind to repay the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Yuezhi heir had become king; having already struck Great Bactria, they divided its lands and dwelt there; the land was rich and fertile, with few raids, and utterly without a mind to repay the Hu.

sentences.zh: 騫留歲餘，竟不能得月氏要領，乃還；

translations.literal: Qian remained more than a year; in the end he could not obtain the Yuezhi's essential point, and then returned;
translations.idiomatic: Qian remained more than a year; in the end he could not obtain the Yuezhi's essential point, and then returned;

sentences.zh: 並南山，欲從羌中歸，復為匈奴所得，留歲餘。

translations.literal: along the southern mountains he wished to return through the Qiang lands, but was again obtained by the Xiongnu and detained more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: along the southern mountains he wished to return through the Qiang lands, but was again seized by the Xiongnu and detained more than a year.

sentences.zh: 會伊稚斜逐於單，匈奴國內亂，騫乃與堂邑氏奴甘父逃歸。

translations.literal: It happened that Yizhixie drove out Yu Shan; within the Xiongnu state there was disorder, and Qian then with the Tangyi clan slave Ganfu fled and returned.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Yizhixie drove out Yu Shan; within the Xiongnu state there was disorder, and Qian then fled back with the Tangyi clan slave Ganfu.

sentences.zh: 上拜騫為太中大夫，甘父為奉使君。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Qian Palace Grandee in Attendance and Ganfu Envoy Lord.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Qian Palace Grandee in Attendance and Ganfu Envoy Lord.

sentences.zh: 騫初行時百餘人，去十三歲，唯二人得還。

translations.literal: When Qian first set out there were more than a hundred men; he was gone thirteen years, and only two men returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian first set out there were more than a hundred men; he was gone thirteen years, and only two men returned.

sentences.zh: ----6匈奴數萬騎入塞，殺代郡太守恭，及略千餘人。

translations.literal: ----6 The Xiongnu with several tens of thousands of horsemen entered the passes, killed Dai commandery governor Gong, and carried off more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 The Xiongnu with several tens of thousands of horsemen entered the passes, killed Dai commandery governor Gong, and carried off more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: ----7六月，庚午，皇太后崩。

translations.literal: ----7 In the sixth month, on gengwu, the Empress Dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 In the sixth month, on gengwu, the Empress Dowager died.

sentences.zh: ----8秋，罷西夷，獨置南夷、夜郎兩縣、一都尉，稍令犍為自葆就，專力城朔方。

translations.literal: ----8 In autumn, the western Yi were abandoned; only two counties of the southern Yi and Yelang and one commandant were kept; gradually Qian was ordered to protect itself and settle, concentrating effort on walling Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 In autumn, the western Yi were abandoned; only two counties of the southern Yi and Yelang and one commandant were kept; gradually Jian was ordered to protect itself and settle, concentrating effort on walling Shuofang.

sentences.zh: ----9匈奴又入鴈門，殺略千餘人。

translations.literal: ----9 The Xiongnu again entered Yanmen, killing and carrying off more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: ----9 The Xiongnu again entered Yanmen, killing and carrying off more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: ----10是歲，中大夫張湯為廷尉。

translations.literal: ----10 This year, Palace Grandee Zhang Tang was made Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: ----10 This year, Palace Grandee Zhang Tang was made Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 湯為人多詐，舞智以御人。

translations.literal: Tang as a man was much given to fraud, brandishing cleverness to control others.
translations.idiomatic: Tang as a man was much given to fraud, brandishing cleverness to control others.

sentences.zh: 時上方嚮文學，湯陽浮慕，事董仲舒、公孫弘等。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor above was turning toward literary studies; Tang outwardly floated in admiration and served Dong Zhongshu, Gongsun Hong, and others.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was turning toward literary studies; Tang outwardly feigned admiration and cultivated Dong Zhongshu, Gongsun Hong, and others.

sentences.zh: 以千乘兒寬為奏讞掾，以古法義決疑獄。

translations.literal: He made Ni Kuan of Qiansheng his memorial-recommendation aide and used ancient law and righteousness to decide doubtful cases.
translations.idiomatic: He made Ni Kuan of Qiansheng his memorial-recommendation aide and used ancient law and righteousness to decide doubtful cases.

sentences.zh: 所治，即上意所欲罪，與監、史深禍者；

translations.literal: What he tried—if it matched what the emperor above wished to punish, he joined with supervisors and clerks who deepened calamity;
translations.idiomatic: What he tried—if it matched what the emperor wished to punish, he joined with supervisors and clerks who deepened calamity;

sentences.zh: 即上意所欲釋，與監、史輕平者；

translations.literal: if it matched what the emperor above wished to release, he joined with supervisors and clerks who were light and even;
translations.idiomatic: if it matched what the emperor wished to release, he joined with supervisors and clerks who were lenient and even;

sentences.zh: 上由是悅之。

translations.literal: the emperor thereby was pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor thereby was pleased with him.

sentences.zh: 湯於故人子弟調護之尤厚；

translations.literal: Tang toward old friends' sons and younger brothers was especially thick in care and protection;
translations.idiomatic: Tang toward old friends' sons and younger brothers was especially generous in care and protection;

sentences.zh: 其造請諸公，不避寒暑。

translations.literal: when he went to call on the great lords, he did not avoid cold or heat.
translations.idiomatic: when he went to call on the great lords, he did not avoid cold or heat.

sentences.zh: 是以湯雖文深、意忌、不專平，然得此聲譽。

translations.literal: Therefore although Tang was literary-deep, intent-jealous, and not solely even, yet he obtained this fame and praise.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore although Tang was literary in depth, jealous in intent, and not solely even-handed, yet he obtained this fame and praise.

sentences.zh: 汲黯數質責湯於上前曰：「公為正卿，上不能褒先帝之功業，下不能抑天下之邪心，安國富民，使囹圄空虛，何空取高皇帝約束紛更之為！

translations.literal: Ji An several times directly reproached Tang before the emperor, saying: "Sir, as chief minister, above you cannot praise the former emperor's achievements and enterprise, below you cannot restrain the world's wicked hearts, settle the state and enrich the people, and make the prisons empty—why vainly take the High Emperor's covenants and change them in confusion!
translations.idiomatic: Ji An several times directly reproached Tang before the emperor, saying, "Sir, as chief minister, above you cannot praise the former emperor's achievements, below you cannot restrain the world's wicked hearts, settle the state and enrich the people, and make the prisons empty—why vainly take the High Emperor's covenants and change them in confusion!

sentences.zh: 而公以此無種矣。

translations.literal: Yet you will thereby have no posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you will thereby have no posterity.

sentences.zh: 」黯時與湯論議，湯辯常在文深小苛；

translations.literal: " When An at times debated with Tang, Tang's disputation was always in literary depth and petty harshness;
translations.idiomatic: " When An at times debated with Tang, Tang's disputation was always literary in depth and petty in harshness;

sentences.zh: 黯伉厲守高，不能屈，忿發，罵曰：「天下謂刀筆吏不可以為公卿，果然！

translations.literal: An was stern and lofty, holding high and could not be bent; anger burst forth and he cursed, saying: "All under Heaven says clerk-scribes cannot be made chief ministers—truly so!
translations.idiomatic: An was stern and lofty, holding high and could not be bent; anger burst forth and he cursed, saying, "All under Heaven says clerk-scribes cannot be made chief ministers—truly so!

sentences.zh: 必湯也，令天下重足而立，側目而視矣！

translations.literal: It must be Tang—he will make all under Heaven stand with both feet heavy and look with sidelong eyes!
translations.idiomatic: It must be Tang—he will make all under Heaven stand with both feet heavy and look with sidelong eyes!

sentences.zh: 1冬，上行幸甘泉。

translations.literal: 1 In winter, the emperor traveled in person to Ganquan.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In winter, the emperor traveled in person to Ganquan.

sentences.zh: ----2夏，匈奴入代郡、定襄、上郡，各三萬騎，殺略數千人。

translations.literal: ----2 In summer, the Xiongnu entered Dai commandery, Dingxiang, and Shang commandery, each with thirty thousand horsemen, killing and carrying off several thousands.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In summer, the Xiongnu entered Dai commandery, Dingxiang, and Shang commandery, each with thirty thousand horsemen, killing and carrying off several thousands.
